# ============================================================================
# 1. TOKENIZATION PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class Tokenizer:
    """
    Advanced tokenization pattern supporting multiple tokenization strategies.
    Converts raw text into token sequences.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        vocab_size: int = 10000,
        min_freq: int = 1,
        special_tokens: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        lowercase: bool = True
    ):
        """
        Args:
            vocab_size: Maximum vocabulary size
            min_freq: Minimum frequency for a token to be included
            special_tokens: Special tokens like [PAD], [UNK], [CLS], [SEP]
            lowercase: Whether to convert text to lowercase
        """
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.min_freq = min_freq
        self.lowercase = lowercase
        
        # Initialize special tokens
        self.special_tokens = special_tokens or ['[PAD]', '[UNK]', '[CLS]', '[SEP]']
        self.token2idx = {token: idx for idx, token in enumerate(self.special_tokens)}
        self.idx2token = {idx: token for token, idx in self.token2idx.items()}
        
        self.pad_token = '[PAD]'
        self.unk_token = '[UNK]'
        self.cls_token = '[CLS]'
        self.sep_token = '[SEP]'
        
        self.vocab_built = False
    
    def tokenize(self, text: str) -> List[str]:
        """
        Basic word tokenization with regex.
        
        Args:
            text: Input text string
            
        Returns:
            List of tokens
        """
        if self.lowercase:
            text = text.lower()
        
        # Simple word tokenization (can be replaced with more sophisticated methods)
        tokens = re.findall(r'\b\w+\b|[^\w\s]', text)
        return tokens
    
    def build_vocab(self, texts: List[str]):
        """
        Build vocabulary from a corpus of texts.
        
        Args:
            texts: List of text strings
        """
        # Tokenize all texts and count frequencies
        token_freq = Counter()
        for text in texts:
            tokens = self.tokenize(text)
            token_freq.update(tokens)
        
        # Filter by minimum frequency and sort by frequency
        filtered_tokens = [
            token for token, freq in token_freq.items() 
            if freq >= self.min_freq and token not in self.special_tokens
        ]
        
        # Sort by frequency (descending) and limit to vocab_size
        sorted_tokens = sorted(
            filtered_tokens,
            key=lambda x: token_freq[x],
            reverse=True
        )[:self.vocab_size - len(self.special_tokens)]
        
        # Build token2idx and idx2token mappings
        for token in sorted_tokens:
            idx = len(self.token2idx)
            self.token2idx[token] = idx
            self.idx2token[idx] = token
        
        self.vocab_built = True
        print(f"Vocabulary built with {len(self.token2idx)} tokens")
    
    def encode(
        self,
        text: str,
        max_length: Optional[int] = None,
        padding: bool = False,
        truncation: bool = False,
        add_special_tokens: bool = False
    ) -> List[int]:
        """
        Encode text to token indices.
        
        Args:
            text: Input text
            max_length: Maximum sequence length
            padding: Whether to pad to max_length
            truncation: Whether to truncate to max_length
            add_special_tokens: Whether to add [CLS] and [SEP] tokens
            
        Returns:
            List of token indices
        """
        if not self.vocab_built:
            raise ValueError("Vocabulary not built. Call build_vocab() first.")
        
        tokens = self.tokenize(text)
        
        # Add special tokens
        if add_special_tokens:
            tokens = [self.cls_token] + tokens + [self.sep_token]
        
        # Convert tokens to indices
        indices = [
            self.token2idx.get(token, self.token2idx[self.unk_token])
            for token in tokens
        ]
        
        # Truncation
        if truncation and max_length and len(indices) > max_length:
            indices = indices[:max_length]
        
        # Padding
        if padding and max_length:
            pad_length = max_length - len(indices)
            if pad_length > 0:
                indices = indices + [self.token2idx[self.pad_token]] * pad_length
        
        return indices
    
    def decode(self, indices: List[int], skip_special_tokens: bool = True) -> str:
        """
        Decode token indices back to text.
        
        Args:
            indices: List of token indices
            skip_special_tokens: Whether to skip special tokens
            
        Returns:
            Decoded text string
        """
        tokens = []
        for idx in indices:
            token = self.idx2token.get(idx, self.unk_token)
            if skip_special_tokens and token in self.special_tokens:
                continue
            tokens.append(token)
        
        return ' '.join(tokens)
    
    def batch_encode(
        self,
        texts: List[str],
        max_length: Optional[int] = None,
        padding: bool = True,
        truncation: bool = True,
        add_special_tokens: bool = True
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Batch encode multiple texts.
        
        Args:
            texts: List of text strings
            max_length: Maximum sequence length
            padding: Whether to pad sequences
            truncation: Whether to truncate sequences
            add_special_tokens: Whether to add special tokens
            
        Returns:
            Tensor of shape (batch_size, max_length)
        """
        encoded = [
            self.encode(
                text,
                max_length=max_length,
                padding=padding,
                truncation=truncation,
                add_special_tokens=add_special_tokens
            )
            for text in texts
        ]
        
        return torch.tensor(encoded, dtype=torch.long)

# 2. NORMALIZATION PIPELINE PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class NormalizationPipeline:
    """
    Flexible normalization pipeline that applies multiple normalization
    steps in sequence. Supports composition of different normalization techniques.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.steps: List[Tuple[str, Callable]] = []
        self.fitted = False
        self.stats = {}
    
    def add_step(self, name: str, transform_fn: Callable) -> 'NormalizationPipeline':
        """
        Add a normalization step to the pipeline.
        
        Args:
            name: Name of the step
            transform_fn: Function that performs the transformation
            
        Returns:
            Self for method chaining
        """
        self.steps.append((name, transform_fn))
        return self
    
    def fit(self, data: torch.Tensor) -> 'NormalizationPipeline':
        """
        Fit the pipeline on training data to compute statistics.
        
        Args:
            data: Training data tensor
            
        Returns:
            Self for method chaining
        """
        # Compute statistics for each normalization method
        self.stats['mean'] = data.mean(dim=0)
        self.stats['std'] = data.std(dim=0) + 1e-8  # Add epsilon for numerical stability
        self.stats['min'] = data.min(dim=0)[0]
        self.stats['max'] = data.max(dim=0)[0]
        self.stats['median'] = data.median(dim=0)[0]
        self.stats['q25'] = torch.quantile(data, 0.25, dim=0)
        self.stats['q75'] = torch.quantile(data, 0.75, dim=0)
        
        self.fitted = True
        return self
    
    def transform(self, data: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Apply all normalization steps to the data.
        
        Args:
            data: Input data tensor
            
        Returns:
            Normalized data tensor
        """
        if not self.fitted:
            raise ValueError("Pipeline not fitted. Call fit() first.")
        
        result = data.clone()
        for name, transform_fn in self.steps:
            result = transform_fn(result, self.stats)
        
        return result
    
    def fit_transform(self, data: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Fit and transform in one step.
        
        Args:
            data: Input data tensor
            
        Returns:
            Normalized data tensor
        """
        self.fit(data)
        return self.transform(data)


# Predefined normalization functions
class Normalizations:
    """Collection of common normalization functions."""
    
    @staticmethod
    def standardize(data: torch.Tensor, stats: Dict) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Z-score normalization: (x - mean) / std"""
        return (data - stats['mean']) / stats['std']
    
    @staticmethod
    def min_max_normalize(data: torch.Tensor, stats: Dict) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Min-max normalization: (x - min) / (max - min)"""
        return (data - stats['min']) / (stats['max'] - stats['min'] + 1e-8)
    
    @staticmethod
    def robust_normalize(data: torch.Tensor, stats: Dict) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Robust normalization using median and IQR"""
        iqr = stats['q75'] - stats['q25'] + 1e-8
        return (data - stats['median']) / iqr
    
    @staticmethod
    def l2_normalize(data: torch.Tensor, stats: Dict) -> torch.Tensor:
        """L2 normalization: x / ||x||_2"""
        return F.normalize(data, p=2, dim=-1)
    
    @staticmethod
    def clip_normalize(
        data: torch.Tensor,
        stats: Dict,
        clip_min: float = -3.0,
        clip_max: float = 3.0
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Clip values and then normalize"""
        clipped = torch.clamp(data, clip_min, clip_max)
        return (clipped - stats['mean']) / stats['std']

class FeatureScaler(nn.Module):
    """
    Advanced feature scaling module with multiple scaling strategies.
    Can be integrated into PyTorch models as a layer.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        num_features: int,
        method: str = 'standard',
        learnable: bool = False
    ):
        """
        Args:
            num_features: Number of features to scale
            method: Scaling method ('standard', 'minmax', 'robust', 'maxabs')
            learnable: Whether scaling parameters are learnable
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.num_features = num_features
        self.method = method
        self.learnable = learnable
        
        # Initialize scaling parameters
        if learnable:
            self.scale = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(num_features))
            self.shift = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(num_features))
        else:
            self.register_buffer('scale', torch.ones(num_features))
            self.register_buffer('shift', torch.zeros(num_features))
        
        # Statistics buffers
        self.register_buffer('running_mean', torch.zeros(num_features))
        self.register_buffer('running_var', torch.ones(num_features))
        self.register_buffer('running_min', torch.zeros(num_features))
        self.register_buffer('running_max', torch.ones(num_features))
        self.register_buffer('num_batches_tracked', torch.tensor(0, dtype=torch.long))
        
        self.momentum = 0.1
        self.eps = 1e-8
    
    def update_statistics(self, x: torch.Tensor):
        """Update running statistics during training."""
        if self.training:
            with torch.no_grad():
                batch_mean = x.mean(dim=0)
                batch_var = x.var(dim=0, unbiased=False)
                batch_min = x.min(dim=0)[0]
                batch_max = x.max(dim=0)[0]
                
                # Exponential moving average
                self.running_mean = (
                    (1 - self.momentum) * self.running_mean +
                    self.momentum * batch_mean
                )
                self.running_var = (
                    (1 - self.momentum) * self.running_var +
                    self.momentum * batch_var
                )
                self.running_min = torch.min(self.running_min, batch_min)
                self.running_max = torch.max(self.running_max, batch_max)
                
                self.num_batches_tracked += 1
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Apply feature scaling.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, num_features)
            
        Returns:
            Scaled tensor
        """
        self.update_statistics(x)
        
        if self.method == 'standard':
            # Standard scaling: (x - mean) / std
            mean = self.running_mean if not self.training else x.mean(dim=0)
            std = torch.sqrt(self.running_var + self.eps)
            scaled = (x - mean) / std
            
        elif self.method == 'minmax':
            # Min-max scaling: (x - min) / (max - min)
            min_val = self.running_min
            max_val = self.running_max
            scaled = (x - min_val) / (max_val - min_val + self.eps)
            
        elif self.method == 'robust':
            # Robust scaling using median and IQR
            median = x.median(dim=0)[0] if self.training else self.running_mean
            q75 = torch.quantile(x, 0.75, dim=0) if self.training else self.running_max
            q25 = torch.quantile(x, 0.25, dim=0) if self.training else self.running_min
            iqr = q75 - q25 + self.eps
            scaled = (x - median) / iqr
            
        elif self.method == 'maxabs':
            # Max absolute scaling: x / max(|x|)
            max_abs = torch.max(torch.abs(self.running_min), torch.abs(self.running_max))
            scaled = x / (max_abs + self.eps)
            
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown scaling method: {self.method}")
        
        # Apply learnable affine transformation if enabled
        if self.learnable:

```python
        # Apply learnable affine transformation if enabled
        if self.learnable:
            scaled = scaled * self.scale + self.shift
        
        return scaled
    
    def inverse_transform(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Inverse transformation to get back original scale.
        
        Args:
            x: Scaled tensor
            
        Returns:
            Original scale tensor
        """
        # Reverse learnable transformation first
        if self.learnable:
            x = (x - self.shift) / (self.scale + self.eps)
        
        if self.method == 'standard':
            std = torch.sqrt(self.running_var + self.eps)
            original = x * std + self.running_mean
            
        elif self.method == 'minmax':
            original = x * (self.running_max - self.running_min) + self.running_min
            
        elif self.method == 'robust':
            iqr = self.running_max - self.running_min
            original = x * iqr + self.running_mean
            
        elif self.method == 'maxabs':
            max_abs = torch.max(torch.abs(self.running_min), torch.abs(self.running_max))
            original = x * max_abs
            
        return original

# 4. ONE-HOT ENCODING PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class OneHotEncoder(nn.Module):
    """
    One-hot encoding module for categorical variables.
    Supports both static and dynamic encoding with optional smoothing.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        num_classes: int,
        smooth: bool = False,
        smoothing_factor: float = 0.1,
        sparse: bool = False
    ):
        """
        Args:
            num_classes: Number of categories
            smooth: Whether to apply label smoothing
            smoothing_factor: Smoothing factor for label smoothing
            sparse: Whether to return sparse tensors
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.smooth = smooth
        self.smoothing_factor = smoothing_factor
        self.sparse = sparse
    
    def forward(self, indices: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Convert indices to one-hot encoded vectors.
        
        Args:
            indices: Tensor of indices, shape (batch_size,) or (batch_size, seq_len)
            
        Returns:
            One-hot encoded tensor
        """
        # Ensure indices are long type
        indices = indices.long()
        
        # Get shape information
        original_shape = indices.shape
        indices_flat = indices.view(-1)
        
        # Create one-hot encoding
        one_hot = torch.zeros(
            indices_flat.size(0),
            self.num_classes,
            device=indices.device,
            dtype=torch.float32
        )
        one_hot.scatter_(1, indices_flat.unsqueeze(1), 1.0)
        
        # Apply label smoothing if enabled
        if self.smooth:
            one_hot = one_hot * (1 - self.smoothing_factor) + \
                     self.smoothing_factor / self.num_classes
        
        # Reshape to original dimensions plus num_classes
        output_shape = original_shape + (self.num_classes,)
        one_hot = one_hot.view(*output_shape)
        
        # Convert to sparse if requested
        if self.sparse:
            one_hot = one_hot.to_sparse()
        
        return one_hot
    
    def encode_multiple(
        self,
        indices_list: List[torch.Tensor],
        concat: bool = True
    ) -> Union[torch.Tensor, List[torch.Tensor]]:
        """
        Encode multiple categorical variables.
        
        Args:
            indices_list: List of index tensors
            concat: Whether to concatenate all encodings
            
        Returns:
            Encoded tensor(s)
        """
        encoded = [self.forward(indices) for indices in indices_list]
        
        if concat:
            return torch.cat(encoded, dim=-1)
        return encoded


class MultiCategoricalEncoder(nn.Module):
    """
    Encoder for multiple categorical features with different cardinalities.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        cardinalities: List[int],
        smooth: bool = False,
        smoothing_factor: float = 0.1
    ):
        """
        Args:
            cardinalities: List of number of categories for each feature
            smooth: Whether to apply label smoothing
            smoothing_factor: Smoothing factor for label smoothing
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.cardinalities = cardinalities
        self.encoders = nn.ModuleList([
            OneHotEncoder(num_classes=card, smooth=smooth, smoothing_factor=smoothing_factor)
            for card in cardinalities
        ])
    
    def forward(self, categorical_inputs: List[torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Encode multiple categorical features and concatenate.
        
        Args:
            categorical_inputs: List of categorical input tensors
            
        Returns:
            Concatenated one-hot encoded tensor
        """
        if len(categorical_inputs) != len(self.encoders):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected {len(self.encoders)} categorical inputs, "
                f"got {len(categorical_inputs)}"
            )
        
        encoded = [
            encoder(inputs)
            for encoder, inputs in zip(self.encoders, categorical_inputs)
        ]
        
        return torch.cat(encoded, dim=-1)

class EmbeddingLookup(nn.Module):
    """
    Advanced embedding lookup with multiple features:
    - Pretrained embeddings
    - Position embeddings
    - Segment embeddings
    - Dropout and layer normalization
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        vocab_size: int,
        embedding_dim: int,
        max_position: int = 512,
        num_segments: int = 2,
        padding_idx: Optional[int] = 0,
        pretrained_embeddings: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        freeze_embeddings: bool = False,
        dropout: float = 0.1,
        use_layer_norm: bool = True,
        scale_embeddings: bool = True
    ):
        """
        Args:
            vocab_size: Size of vocabulary
            embedding_dim: Dimension of embeddings
            max_position: Maximum position for position embeddings
            num_segments: Number of segment types
            padding_idx: Index for padding token
            pretrained_embeddings: Pretrained embedding matrix
            freeze_embeddings: Whether to freeze token embeddings
            dropout: Dropout probability
            use_layer_norm: Whether to apply layer normalization
            scale_embeddings: Whether to scale embeddings by sqrt(d)
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.embedding_dim = embedding_dim
        self.padding_idx = padding_idx
        self.scale_embeddings = scale_embeddings
        
        # Token embeddings
        if pretrained_embeddings is not None:
            self.token_embeddings = nn.Embedding.from_pretrained(
                pretrained_embeddings,
                freeze=freeze_embeddings,
                padding_idx=padding_idx
            )
        else:
            self.token_embeddings = nn.Embedding(
                vocab_size,
                embedding_dim,
                padding_idx=padding_idx
            )
        
        # Position embeddings
        self.position_embeddings = nn.Embedding(max_position, embedding_dim)
        
        # Segment embeddings (for tasks like sentence pair classification)
        self.segment_embeddings = nn.Embedding(num_segments, embedding_dim)
        
        # Layer normalization and dropout
        self.use_layer_norm = use_layer_norm
        if use_layer_norm:
            self.layer_norm = nn.LayerNorm(embedding_dim)
        
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        
        # Scaling factor
        if scale_embeddings:
            self.scale = torch.sqrt(torch.tensor(embedding_dim, dtype=torch.float32))
        else:
            self.scale = 1.0
    
    def forward(
        self,
        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
        position_ids: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        segment_ids: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Lookup and combine embeddings.
        
        Args:
            input_ids: Token indices, shape (batch_size, seq_len)
            position_ids: Position indices, shape (batch_size, seq_len)
            segment_ids: Segment indices, shape (batch_size, seq_len)
            
        Returns:
            Combined embeddings, shape (batch_size, seq_len, embedding_dim)
        """
        batch_size, seq_len = input_ids.shape
        
        # Get token embeddings
        token_embeds = self.token_embeddings(input_ids)
        
        # Scale embeddings if enabled
        if self.scale_embeddings:
            token_embeds = token_embeds * self.scale
        
        # Get position embeddings
        if position_ids is None:
            position_ids = torch.arange(
                seq_len,
                dtype=torch.long,
                device=input_ids.device
            ).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch_size, -1)
        
        position_embeds = self.position_embeddings(position_ids)
        
        # Combine embeddings
        embeddings = token_embeds + position_embeds
        
        # Add segment embeddings if provided
        if segment_ids is not None:
            segment_embeds = self.segment_embeddings(segment_ids)
            embeddings = embeddings + segment_embeds
        
        # Apply layer normalization
        if self.use_layer_norm:
            embeddings = self.layer_norm(embeddings)
        
        # Apply dropout
        embeddings = self.dropout(embeddings)
        
        return embeddings
    
    def get_token_embedding(self, token_id: int) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Get embedding for a specific token."""
        return self.token_embeddings.weight[token_id]
    
    def get_similar_tokens(
        self,
        token_id: int,
        top_k: int = 10
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Find most similar tokens based on embedding similarity.
        
        Args:
            token_id: Query token ID
            top_k: Number of similar tokens to return
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (similarity_scores, token_indices)
        """
        query_embed = self.token_embeddings.weight[token_id]
        
        # Compute cosine similarity with all embeddings
        all_embeds = self.token_embeddings.weight
        similarities = F.cosine_similarity(
            query_embed.unsqueeze(0),
            all_embeds,
            dim=-1
        )
        
        # Get top-k most similar
        top_similarities, top_indices = torch.topk(similarities, k=top_k + 1)
        
        # Exclude the query token itself
        mask = top_indices != token_id
        top_similarities = top_similarities[mask][:top_k]
        top_indices = top_indices[mask][:top_k]
        
        return top_similarities, top_indices

# 6. BATCH ENCODING PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class BatchEncoder:
    """
    Efficient batch encoding with dynamic padding and attention masks.
    Handles variable-length sequences in batches.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        pad_token_id: int = 0,
        max_length: Optional[int] = None,
        padding_side: str = 'right',
        truncation_side: str = 'right'
    ):
        """
        Args:
            pad_token_id: ID of padding token
            max_length: Maximum sequence length
            padding_side: Side to add padding ('left' or 'right')
            truncation_side: Side to truncate ('left' or 'right')
        """
        self.pad_token_id = pad_token_id
        self.max_length = max_length
        self.padding_side = padding_side
        self.truncation_side = truncation_side
    
    def encode_batch(
        self,
        sequences: List[List[int]],
        return_tensors: bool = True,
        return_attention_mask: bool = True,
        return_length: bool = False
    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Encode a batch of sequences with padding and attention masks.
        
        Args:
            sequences: List of token ID sequences
            return_tensors: Whether to return PyTorch tensors
            return_attention_mask: Whether to return attention masks
            return_length: Whether to return original lengths
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing encoded data
        """
        # Determine batch max length
        lengths = [len(seq) for seq in sequences]
        batch_max_len = max(lengths)
        
        if self.max_length is not None:
            batch_max_len = min(batch_max_len, self.max_length)
        
        # Initialize output lists
        padded_sequences = []
        attention_masks = []
        
        for seq in sequences:
            # Truncate if necessary
            if len(seq) > batch_max_len:
                if self.truncation_side == 'right':
                    seq = seq[:batch_max_len]
                else:  # left
                    seq = seq[-batch_max_len:]
            
            # Create attention mask (1 for real tokens, 0 for padding)
            attention_mask = [1] * len(seq)
            
            # Pad sequence
            padding_length = batch_max_len - len(seq)
            if padding_length > 0:
                if self.padding_side == 'right':
                    seq = seq + [self.pad_token_id] * padding_length
                    attention_mask = attention_mask + [0] * padding_length
                else:  # left
                    seq = [self.pad_token_id] * padding_length + seq
                    attention_mask = [0] * padding_length + attention_mask
            
            padded_sequences.append(seq)
            attention_masks.append(attention_mask)
        
        # Prepare output dictionary
        output = {}
        
        if return_tensors:
            output['input_ids'] = torch.tensor(padded_sequences, dtype=torch.long)
            if return_attention_mask:
                output['attention_mask'] = torch.tensor(attention_masks, dtype=torch.long)
        else:
            output['input_ids'] = padded_sequences
            if return_attention_mask:
                output['attention_mask'] = attention_masks
        
        if return_length:
            output['length'] = torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.long) if return_tensors else lengths
        
        return output
    
    def create_position_ids(
        self,
        attention_mask: torch.Tensor,
        past_key_values_length: int = 0
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Create position IDs from attention mask.
        
        Args:
            attention_mask: Attention mask tensor
            past_key_values_length: Length of cached past key values
            
        Returns:
            Position IDs tensor
        """
        # Create position IDs, accounting for padding
        position_ids = attention_mask.cumsum(dim=-1) - 
```python
        # Create position IDs, accounting for padding
        position_ids = attention_mask.cumsum(dim=-1) - 1
        position_ids.masked_fill_(attention_mask == 0, 0)
        
        # Add offset for past key values
        if past_key_values_length > 0:
            position_ids = position_ids + past_key_values_length
        
        return position_ids
    
    def create_causal_mask(
        self,
        batch_size: int,
        seq_len: int,
        device: torch.device
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Create causal (autoregressive) attention mask.
        
        Args:
            batch_size: Batch size
            seq_len: Sequence length
            device: Device to create tensor on
            
        Returns:
            Causal mask tensor of shape (batch_size, 1, seq_len, seq_len)
        """
        # Create lower triangular matrix
        mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len, device=device))
        # Expand for batch and heads
        mask = mask.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch_size, 1, seq_len, seq_len)
        return mask
    
    def merge_masks(
        self,
        attention_mask: torch.Tensor,
        causal_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Merge padding mask with causal mask.
        
        Args:
            attention_mask: Padding attention mask (batch_size, seq_len)
            causal_mask: Causal attention mask (batch_size, 1, seq_len, seq_len)
            
        Returns:
            Combined mask
        """
        # Expand attention mask to 4D
        # (batch_size, seq_len) -> (batch_size, 1, 1, seq_len)
        expanded_mask = attention_mask.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(2)
        
        # Convert to float and create additive mask
        # 1 -> 0.0 (attend), 0 -> -inf (don't attend)
        expanded_mask = (1.0 - expanded_mask) * torch.finfo(torch.float32).min
        
        if causal_mask is not None:
            # Combine with causal mask
            causal_mask = (1.0 - causal_mask) * torch.finfo(torch.float32).min
            combined_mask = expanded_mask + causal_mask
            return combined_mask
        
        return expanded_mask


class DynamicBatchCollator:
    """
    Dynamic batch collator for DataLoader that handles variable-length sequences
    and multiple input types.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        pad_token_id: int = 0,
        pad_values: Optional[Dict[str, float]] = None,
        return_attention_mask: bool = True
    ):
        """
        Args:
            pad_token_id: Padding token ID for sequences
            pad_values: Dictionary of padding values for different fields
            return_attention_mask: Whether to create attention masks
        """
        self.pad_token_id = pad_token_id
        self.pad_values = pad_values or {}
        self.return_attention_mask = return_attention_mask
    
    def __call__(self, batch: List[Dict[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Collate batch with dynamic padding.
        
        Args:
            batch: List of sample dictionaries
            
        Returns:
            Batched dictionary with padded tensors
        """
        if not batch:
            return {}
        
        # Get all keys from first sample
        keys = batch[0].keys()
        collated = {}
        
        for key in keys:
            # Extract all values for this key
            values = [sample[key] for sample in batch]
            
            # Handle different data types
            if isinstance(values[0], torch.Tensor):
                if values[0].dim() == 0:
                    # Scalar tensors - just stack
                    collated[key] = torch.stack(values)
                elif values[0].dim() == 1:
                    # 1D tensors - pad and stack
                    collated[key] = self._pad_sequences(values, key)
                else:
                    # Higher dimensional tensors - pad if needed
                    collated[key] = self._pad_tensors(values, key)
            elif isinstance(values[0], (int, float)):
                # Numeric values - convert to tensor
                collated[key] = torch.tensor(values)
            else:
                # Keep as list for other types
                collated[key] = values
        
        # Add attention mask if requested
        if self.return_attention_mask and 'input_ids' in collated:
            collated['attention_mask'] = (
                collated['input_ids'] != self.pad_token_id
            ).long()
        
        return collated
    
    def _pad_sequences(
        self,
        sequences: List[torch.Tensor],
        key: str
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Pad 1D sequences to same length."""
        max_len = max(seq.size(0) for seq in sequences)
        pad_value = self.pad_values.get(key, self.pad_token_id)
        
        padded = []
        for seq in sequences:
            padding = max_len - seq.size(0)
            if padding > 0:
                pad_seq = torch.cat([
                    seq,
                    torch.full((padding,), pad_value, dtype=seq.dtype, device=seq.device)
                ])
            else:
                pad_seq = seq
            padded.append(pad_seq)
        
        return torch.stack(padded)
    
    def _pad_tensors(
        self,
        tensors: List[torch.Tensor],
        key: str
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Pad higher dimensional tensors."""
        # Find maximum size in each dimension
        max_shape = list(tensors[0].shape)
        for tensor in tensors[1:]:
            for i, size in enumerate(tensor.shape):
                max_shape[i] = max(max_shape[i], size)
        
        pad_value = self.pad_values.get(key, 0.0)
        
        padded = []
        for tensor in tensors:
            # Calculate padding needed
            padding = []
            for i in range(len(max_shape) - 1, -1, -1):
                diff = max_shape[i] - tensor.shape[i]
                padding.extend([0, diff])
            
            # Apply padding
            if any(p > 0 for p in padding):
                padded_tensor = F.pad(tensor, padding, value=pad_value)
            else:
                padded_tensor = tensor
            
            padded.append(padded_tensor)
        
        return torch.stack(padded)

# 7. DYNAMIC PREPROCESSING PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class DynamicPreprocessor(nn.Module):
    """
    Dynamic preprocessing that adapts based on input characteristics.
    Supports conditional preprocessing, data augmentation, and adaptive normalization.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        preprocessing_configs: Optional[Dict] = None,
        adaptive: bool = True
    ):
        """
        Args:
            input_dim: Input dimension
            preprocessing_configs: Configuration for different preprocessing strategies
            adaptive: Whether to adapt preprocessing based on data statistics
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.adaptive = adaptive
        
        # Default preprocessing configurations
        self.configs = preprocessing_configs or {
            'normalize': True,
            'clip': True,
            'augment': False,
            'noise_level': 0.01
        }
        
        # Adaptive statistics
        self.register_buffer('running_mean', torch.zeros(input_dim))
        self.register_buffer('running_std', torch.ones(input_dim))
        self.register_buffer('running_min', torch.zeros(input_dim))
        self.register_buffer('running_max', torch.ones(input_dim))
        self.register_buffer('num_batches', torch.tensor(0, dtype=torch.long))
        
        # Learnable preprocessing parameters
        self.adaptive_scale = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(input_dim))
        self.adaptive_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(input_dim))
        
        # Preprocessing modules
        self.normalizer = nn.BatchNorm1d(input_dim, affine=False)
        
        self.momentum = 0.1
    
    def update_statistics(self, x: torch.Tensor):
        """Update running statistics for adaptive preprocessing."""
        if self.training and self.adaptive:
            with torch.no_grad():
                batch_mean = x.mean(dim=0)
                batch_std = x.std(dim=0)
                batch_min = x.min(dim=0)[0]
                batch_max = x.max(dim=0)[0]
                
                # Update running statistics
                if self.num_batches == 0:
                    self.running_mean = batch_mean
                    self.running_std = batch_std
                    self.running_min = batch_min
                    self.running_max = batch_max
                else:
                    self.running_mean = (
                        (1 - self.momentum) * self.running_mean +
                        self.momentum * batch_mean
                    )
                    self.running_std = (
                        (1 - self.momentum) * self.running_std +
                        self.momentum * batch_std
                    )
                    self.running_min = torch.min(self.running_min, batch_min)
                    self.running_max = torch.max(self.running_max, batch_max)
                
                self.num_batches += 1
    
    def detect_outliers(self, x: torch.Tensor, threshold: float = 3.0) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Detect outliers using z-score method.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            threshold: Z-score threshold for outlier detection
            
        Returns:
            Boolean mask indicating outliers
        """
        z_scores = torch.abs((x - self.running_mean) / (self.running_std + 1e-8))
        outliers = z_scores > threshold
        return outliers
    
    def apply_augmentation(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Apply data augmentation during training.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Augmented tensor
        """
        if not self.training or not self.configs.get('augment', False):
            return x
        
        # Add Gaussian noise
        noise_level = self.configs.get('noise_level', 0.01)
        noise = torch.randn_like(x) * noise_level * self.running_std
        x_aug = x + noise
        
        # Random scaling
        if torch.rand(1).item() > 0.5:
            scale = 1.0 + torch.randn(1).item() * 0.1
            x_aug = x_aug * scale
        
        return x_aug
    
    def clip_values(self, x: torch.Tensor, n_std: float = 3.0) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Clip values to prevent extreme outliers.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            n_std: Number of standard deviations for clipping
            
        Returns:
            Clipped tensor
        """
        if not self.configs.get('clip', False):
            return x
        
        lower_bound = self.running_mean - n_std * self.running_std
        upper_bound = self.running_mean + n_std * self.running_std
        
        return torch.clamp(x, lower_bound, upper_bound)
    
    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        return_stats: bool = False
    ) -> Union[torch.Tensor, Tuple[torch.Tensor, Dict]]:
        """
        Apply dynamic preprocessing pipeline.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, input_dim)
            return_stats: Whether to return preprocessing statistics
            
        Returns:
            Preprocessed tensor and optionally statistics dictionary
        """
        stats = {}
        
        # Update statistics
        self.update_statistics(x)
        
        # Detect outliers
        outlier_mask = self.detect_outliers(x)
        stats['outlier_ratio'] = outlier_mask.float().mean().item()
        
        # Clip extreme values
        x = self.clip_values(x)
        
        # Apply augmentation
        x = self.apply_augmentation(x)
        
        # Normalize
        if self.configs.get('normalize', True):
            # Use running statistics for normalization
            x_normalized = (x - self.running_mean) / (self.running_std + 1e-8)
        else:
            x_normalized = x
        
        # Apply learnable affine transformation
        x_processed = x_normalized * self.adaptive_scale + self.adaptive_bias
        
        # Collect statistics
        stats['mean'] = x.mean().item()
        stats['std'] = x.std().item()
        stats['min'] = x.min().item()
        stats['max'] = x.max().item()
        
        if return_stats:
            return x_processed, stats
        return x_processed
    
    def adapt_to_distribution(self, x: torch.Tensor, num_iterations: int = 10):
        """
        Adapt preprocessing parameters to match target distribution.
        
        Args:
            x: Target distribution samples
            num_iterations: Number of adaptation iterations
        """
        self.train()
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam([self.adaptive_scale, self.adaptive_bias], lr=0.01)
        
        for _ in range(num_iterations):
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            
            # Process input
            x_processed = self.forward(x)
            
            # Loss: encourage unit normal distribution
            mean_loss = x_processed.mean(dim=0).pow(2).mean()
            std_loss = (x_processed.std(dim=0) - 1.0).pow(2).mean()
            
            loss = mean_loss + std_loss
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()


class ConditionalPreprocessor(nn.Module):
    """
    Conditional preprocessing that applies different preprocessing
    strategies based on input conditions or metadata.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        num_conditions: int,
        condition_dim: int = 16
    ):
        """
        Args:
            input_dim: Input feature dimension
            num_conditions: Number of different preprocessing conditions
            condition_dim: Dimension of condition embedding
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.num_conditions = num_conditions
        
        # Condition embedding
        self.condition_embed = nn.Embedding(num_conditions, condition_dim)
        
        # Condition-specific preprocessing parameters
        self.scale_network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(condition_dim, input_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(input_dim * 2, input_dim),
            nn.Softplus()  # Ensure positive scale
        )
        
        self.bias_network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(condition_dim, input_dim * 2),
            nn.R
```python
        self.bias_network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(condition_dim, input_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(input_dim * 2, input_dim)
        )
        
        # Base normalization
        self.base_norm = nn.LayerNorm(input_dim)
    
    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        condition_ids: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Apply conditional preprocessing.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, input_dim)
            condition_ids: Condition indices of shape (batch_size,)
            
        Returns:
            Preprocessed tensor
        """
        # Get condition embeddings
        condition_embeds = self.condition_embed(condition_ids)
        
        # Generate condition-specific scale and bias
        scale = self.scale_network(condition_embeds)
        bias = self.bias_network(condition_embeds)
        
        # Apply base normalization
        x_norm = self.base_norm(x)
        
        # Apply conditional transformation
        x_processed = x_norm * scale + bias
        
        return x_processed

# COMPREHENSIVE EXAMPLE: COMPLETE PREPROCESSING PIPELINE
# ============================================================================

class CompletePreprocessingPipeline(nn.Module):
    """
    Complete preprocessing pipeline combining all patterns.
    Demonstrates how to use all preprocessing patterns together.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        vocab_size: int = 10000,
        embedding_dim: int = 128,
        num_features: int = 64,
        num_categorical_features: int = 3,
        categorical_cardinalities: List[int] = [10, 20, 5],
        max_seq_len: int = 512
    ):
        """
        Args:
            vocab_size: Vocabulary size for text
            embedding_dim: Embedding dimension
            num_features: Number of numerical features
            num_categorical_features: Number of categorical features
            categorical_cardinalities: List of cardinalities for categorical features
            max_seq_len: Maximum sequence length
        """
        super().__init__()
        
        # Text preprocessing components
        self.embedding_lookup = EmbeddingLookup(
            vocab_size=vocab_size,
            embedding_dim=embedding_dim,
            max_position=max_seq_len,
            dropout=0.1,
            use_layer_norm=True
        )
        
        # Numerical feature preprocessing
        self.feature_scaler = FeatureScaler(
            num_features=num_features,
            method='standard',
            learnable=True
        )
        
        # Categorical feature preprocessing
        self.categorical_encoder = MultiCategoricalEncoder(
            cardinalities=categorical_cardinalities,
            smooth=True,
            smoothing_factor=0.1
        )
        
        # Dynamic preprocessing
        self.dynamic_preprocessor = DynamicPreprocessor(
            input_dim=num_features,
            adaptive=True
        )
        
        # Normalization pipeline for complex transformations
        self.norm_pipeline = NormalizationPipeline()
        self.norm_pipeline.add_step('standardize', Normalizations.standardize)
        self.norm_pipeline.add_step('clip', Normalizations.clip_normalize)
        
        # Output dimensions
        self.text_output_dim = embedding_dim
        self.numerical_output_dim = num_features
        self.categorical_output_dim = sum(categorical_cardinalities)
        self.total_output_dim = (
            self.text_output_dim + 
            self.numerical_output_dim + 
            self.categorical_output_dim
        )
    
    def forward(
        self,
        text_input_ids: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        numerical_features: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        categorical_features: Optional[List[torch.Tensor]] = None,
        attention_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Process all input types through the pipeline.
        
        Args:
            text_input_ids: Text token IDs (batch_size, seq_len)
            numerical_features: Numerical features (batch_size, num_features)
            categorical_features: List of categorical feature tensors
            attention_mask: Attention mask for text (batch_size, seq_len)
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing processed features
        """
        outputs = {}
        features_to_concat = []
        
        # Process text input
        if text_input_ids is not None:
            text_embeddings = self.embedding_lookup(text_input_ids)
            
            # Pool embeddings (mean pooling over sequence)
            if attention_mask is not None:
                # Masked mean pooling
                mask_expanded = attention_mask.unsqueeze(-1).expand(text_embeddings.size())
                sum_embeddings = torch.sum(text_embeddings * mask_expanded, dim=1)
                sum_mask = torch.clamp(mask_expanded.sum(dim=1), min=1e-9)
                text_pooled = sum_embeddings / sum_mask
            else:
                text_pooled = text_embeddings.mean(dim=1)
            
            outputs['text_features'] = text_pooled
            features_to_concat.append(text_pooled)
        
        # Process numerical features
        if numerical_features is not None:
            # Apply dynamic preprocessing
            numerical_processed = self.dynamic_preprocessor(numerical_features)
            
            # Apply feature scaling
            numerical_scaled = self.feature_scaler(numerical_processed)
            
            outputs['numerical_features'] = numerical_scaled
            features_to_concat.append(numerical_scaled)
        
        # Process categorical features
        if categorical_features is not None:
            categorical_encoded = self.categorical_encoder(categorical_features)
            
            outputs['categorical_features'] = categorical_encoded
            features_to_concat.append(categorical_encoded)
        
        # Concatenate all features
        if features_to_concat:
            outputs['combined_features'] = torch.cat(features_to_concat, dim=-1)
        
        return outputs

    """Demonstrate normalization pipeline pattern."""
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("NORMALIZATION PIPELINE PATTERN DEMONSTRATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Generate sample data
    torch.manual_seed(42)
    data = torch.randn(100, 10) * 5 + 10
    
    # Create normalization pipeline
    pipeline = NormalizationPipeline()
    pipeline.add_step('standardize', Normalizations.standardize)
    pipeline.add_step('clip', lambda x, stats: torch.clamp(x, -3, 3))
    
    # Fit and transform
    normalized = pipeline.fit_transform(data)
    
    print(f"\nOriginal data stats:")
    print(f"  Mean: {data.mean():.4f}, Std: {data.std():.4f}")
    print(f"  Min: {data.min():.4f}, Max: {data.max():.4f}")
    
    print(f"\nNormalized data stats:")
    print(f"  Mean: {normalized.mean():.4f}, Std: {normalized.std():.4f}")
    print(f"  Min: {normalized.min():.4f}, Max: {normalized.max():.4f}")

class PreprocessedDataset(Dataset):
    """
    Custom dataset that demonstrates integration of preprocessing patterns.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        texts: List[str],
        numerical_features: np.ndarray,
        categorical_features: List[np.ndarray],
        labels: np.ndarray,
        tokenizer: Tokenizer,
        max_length: int = 128
    ):
        """
        Args:
            texts: List of text samples
            numerical_features: Numerical feature array
            categorical_features: List of categorical feature arrays
            labels: Label array
            tokenizer: Tokenizer instance
            max_length: Maximum sequence length
        """
        self.texts = texts
        self.numerical_features = torch.tensor(numerical_features, dtype=torch.float32)
        self.categorical_features = [
            torch.tensor(cat_feat, dtype=torch.long)
            for cat_feat in categorical_features
        ]
        self.labels = torch.tensor(labels, dtype=torch.long)
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.max_length = max_length
    
    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.texts)
    
    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        # Tokenize text
        text_encoded = self.tokenizer.encode(
            self.texts[idx],
            max_length=self.max_length,
            padding=True,
            truncation=True,
            add_special_tokens=True
        )
        
        return {
            'input_ids': torch.tensor(text_encoded, dtype=torch.long),
            'numerical_features': self.numerical_features[idx],
            'categorical_features': [cat[idx] for cat in self.categorical_features],
            'labels': self.labels[idx]
        }

# ADVANCED PREPROCESSING TECHNIQUES
# ============================================================================

class AdaptiveTokenizer(nn.Module):
    """
    Advanced tokenizer with learnable token merging and adaptive vocabulary.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        vocab_size: int,
        embedding_dim: int,
        merge_threshold: float = 0.8
    ):
        """
        Args:
            vocab_size: Initial vocabulary size
            embedding_dim: Embedding dimension
            merge_threshold: Threshold for merging similar tokens
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.embedding_dim = embedding_dim
        self.merge_threshold = merge_threshold
        
        # Token embeddings
        self.embeddings = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embedding_dim)
        
        # Merge score network
        self.merge_scorer = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embedding_dim * 2, embedding_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(embedding_dim, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
    
    def compute_merge_scores(self, token_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute scores for merging adjacent tokens.
        
        Args:
            token_ids: Token ID sequence (seq_len,)
            
        Returns:
            Merge scores for each adjacent pair
        """
        if len(token_ids) < 2:
            return torch.tensor([])
        
        # Get embeddings for all tokens
        embeds = self.embeddings(token_ids)
        
        # Concatenate adjacent token embeddings
        left_embeds = embeds[:-1]
        right_embeds = embeds[1:]
        pair_embeds = torch.cat([left_embeds, right_embeds], dim=-1)
        
        # Compute merge scores
        scores = self.merge_scorer(pair_embeds).squeeze(-1)
        
        return scores
    
    def adaptive_tokenize(
        self,
        token_ids: torch.Tensor
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Adaptively merge tokens based on learned scores.
        
        Args:
            token_ids: Input token IDs
            
        Returns:
            Merged token IDs and merge mask
        """
        merge_scores = self.compute_merge_scores(token_ids)
        
        # Determine which tokens to merge
        should_merge = merge_scores > self.merge_threshold
        
        # Create merged sequence (simplified version)
        merged_ids = []
        merge_mask = []
        i = 0
        
        while i < len(token_ids):
            if i < len(should_merge) and should_merge[i]:
                # Merge with next token (use first token's ID)
                merged_ids.append(token_ids[i])
                merge_mask.append(1)
                i += 2  # Skip next token
            else:
                merged_ids.append(token_ids[i])
                merge_mask.append(0)
                i += 1
        
        return torch.tensor(merged_ids), torch.tensor(merge_mask)


class HierarchicalPreprocessor(nn.Module):
    """
    Hierarchical preprocessing that processes data at multiple scales.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        num_levels: int = 3,
        hidden_dim: int = 64
    ):
        """
        Args:
            input_dim: Input feature dimension
            num_levels: Number of hierarchical levels
            hidden_dim: Hidden dimension for processing
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.num_levels = num_levels
        
        # Preprocessing at each level
        self.level_processors = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Linear(hidden_dim, input_dim)
            )
            for _ in range(num_levels)
        ])
        
        # Aggregation network
        self.aggregator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim * num_levels, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, input_dim)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Process input through hierarchical levels.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor (batch_size, input_dim)
            
        Returns:
            Hierarchically processed tensor
        """
        level_outputs = []
        current = x
        
        # Process at each level
        for processor in self.level_processors:
            processed = processor(current)
            level_outputs.append(processed)
            current = processed
        
        # Aggregate all levels
        combined = torch.cat(level_outputs, dim=-1)
        output = self.aggregator(combined)
        
        return output


class TemporalPreprocessor(nn.Module):
    """
    Preprocessing for temporal/sequential data with time-aware normalization.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        window_size: int = 10,
        use_trend_removal: bool = True
    ):
        """
        Args:
            input_dim: Input feature dimension
            window_size: Window size for moving statistics
            use_trend_removal: Whether to remove trends
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.window_size = window_size
        self.use_trend_removal = use_trend_removal
        
        # Learnable trend parameters
        if use_trend_removal:
            self.trend_network = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv1d(input_dim, input_dim, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Conv1d(input_dim, input_dim, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
            )
        
        # Normalization
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(input_dim)
    
    def compute_moving_stats(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Compute moving mean and std over temporal dimension.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor (batch_size, seq_len, input_dim)
            
        Returns:
            Moving mean and std
        """
        batch_size, seq_len, input_dim = x.shape
        
        # Unfold to create sliding windows
        if seq_len < self.window_size:
            window_size = seq_len
        else:
            window_size = self.window_size
        
        # Compute statistics over windows
        moving_mean = torch.zeros_like(x)
        moving_std = torch.ones_like(x)
        
        for i in range(seq_len):
            start_idx = max(0, i - window_size + 1)
            end_idx = i + 1
            window = x[:, start_idx:end_idx, :]
            
            moving_mean[:, i, :] = window.mean(dim=1)
            moving_std[:, i, :] = window.std(dim=1) + 1e-8
        
        return moving_mean, moving_std
    
    def remove_trend(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Remove trend component from temporal data.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor (batch_size, seq_len, input_dim)
            
        Returns:
            Detrended tensor
        """
        # Transpose for conv1d: (batch, input_dim, seq_len)
        x_transposed = x.transpose(1, 2)
        
        # Estimate trend
        trend = self.trend_network(x_transposed)
        
        # Remove trend
        detrended = x_transposed - trend
        
        # Transpose back
        return detrended.transpose(1, 2)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
```python
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Apply temporal preprocessing.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor (batch_size, seq_len, input_dim)
            
        Returns:
            Preprocessed temporal data
        """
        # Remove trend if enabled
        if self.use_trend_removal:
            x = self.remove_trend(x)
        
        # Compute moving statistics
        moving_mean, moving_std = self.compute_moving_stats(x)
        
        # Normalize using moving statistics
        normalized = (x - moving_mean) / moving_std
        
        # Apply layer normalization
        output = self.norm(normalized)
        
        return output

# PREPROCESSING STRATEGIES FOR DIFFERENT DATA TYPES
# ============================================================================

class MultiModalPreprocessor(nn.Module):
    """
    Preprocessing for multi-modal data (text, image, tabular).
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        text_vocab_size: int = 10000,
        text_embed_dim: int = 128,
        image_channels: int = 3,
        tabular_dim: int = 64,
        output_dim: int = 256
    ):
        """
        Args:
            text_vocab_size: Vocabulary size for text
            text_embed_dim: Text embedding dimension
            image_channels: Number of image channels
            tabular_dim: Dimension of tabular features
            output_dim: Output dimension for all modalities
        """
        super().__init__()
        
        # Text preprocessing
        self.text_embedding = EmbeddingLookup(
            vocab_size=text_vocab_size,
            embedding_dim=text_embed_dim,
            dropout=0.1
        )
        self.text_projection = nn.Linear(text_embed_dim, output_dim)
        
        # Image preprocessing
        self.image_preprocessor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(image_channels, 32, kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1, 1)),
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(64, output_dim)
        )
        
        # Tabular preprocessing
        self.tabular_preprocessor = nn.Sequential(
            FeatureScaler(num_features=tabular_dim, method='standard'),
            nn.Linear(tabular_dim, output_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(output_dim),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # Fusion layer
        self.fusion = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(output_dim * 3, output_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.1),
            nn.Linear(output_dim * 2, output_dim)
        )
    
    def forward(
        self,
        text_ids: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        images: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        tabular: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Process multi-modal inputs.
        
        Args:
            text_ids: Text token IDs (batch_size, seq_len)
            images: Image tensors (batch_size, channels, height, width)
            tabular: Tabular features (batch_size, tabular_dim)
            
        Returns:
            Fused multi-modal representation
        """
        modality_features = []
        
        # Process text
        if text_ids is not None:
            text_embeds = self.text_embedding(text_ids)
            text_pooled = text_embeds.mean(dim=1)
            text_features = self.text_projection(text_pooled)
            modality_features.append(text_features)
        else:
            # Use zero features if modality is missing
            batch_size = images.size(0) if images is not None else tabular.size(0)
            modality_features.append(
                torch.zeros(batch_size, self.fusion[0].in_features // 3, 
                          device=next(self.parameters()).device)
            )
        
        # Process images
        if images is not None:
            image_features = self.image_preprocessor(images)
            modality_features.append(image_features)
        else:
            batch_size = text_ids.size(0) if text_ids is not None else tabular.size(0)
            modality_features.append(
                torch.zeros(batch_size, self.fusion[0].in_features // 3,
                          device=next(self.parameters()).device)
            )
        
        # Process tabular
        if tabular is not None:
            tabular_features = self.tabular_preprocessor(tabular)
            modality_features.append(tabular_features)
        else:
            batch_size = text_ids.size(0) if text_ids is not None else images.size(0)
            modality_features.append(
                torch.zeros(batch_size, self.fusion[0].in_features // 3,
                          device=next(self.parameters()).device)
            )
        
        # Fuse all modalities
        combined = torch.cat(modality_features, dim=-1)
        fused = self.fusion(combined)
        
        return fused


class AugmentationPreprocessor(nn.Module):
    """
    Preprocessing with built-in data augmentation strategies.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        augmentation_prob: float = 0.5,
        noise_std: float = 0.1,
        dropout_prob: float = 0.1,
        mixup_alpha: float = 0.2
    ):
        """
        Args:
            input_dim: Input feature dimension
            augmentation_prob: Probability of applying augmentation
            noise_std: Standard deviation of Gaussian noise
            dropout_prob: Feature dropout probability
            mixup_alpha: Alpha parameter for mixup augmentation
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.augmentation_prob = augmentation_prob
        self.noise_std = noise_std
        self.dropout_prob = dropout_prob
        self.mixup_alpha = mixup_alpha
        
        self.feature_dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_prob)
    
    def add_noise(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Add Gaussian noise to input."""
        if self.training and torch.rand(1).item() < self.augmentation_prob:
            noise = torch.randn_like(x) * self.noise_std
            return x + noise
        return x
    
    def feature_dropout_augment(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Apply feature dropout."""
        if self.training:
            return self.feature_dropout(x)
        return x
    
    def mixup(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        labels: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Optional[torch.Tensor]]:
        """
        Apply mixup augmentation.
        
        Args:
            x: Input features
            labels: Optional labels for mixup
            
        Returns:
            Mixed features and labels
        """
        if not self.training or torch.rand(1).item() >= self.augmentation_prob:
            return x, labels
        
        batch_size = x.size(0)
        
        # Sample mixing coefficient
        lam = np.random.beta(self.mixup_alpha, self.mixup_alpha)
        
        # Generate random permutation
        index = torch.randperm(batch_size, device=x.device)
        
        # Mix inputs
        mixed_x = lam * x + (1 - lam) * x[index]
        
        # Mix labels if provided
        if labels is not None:
            mixed_labels = lam * labels + (1 - lam) * labels[index]
            return mixed_x, mixed_labels
        
        return mixed_x, None
    
    def cutout(self, x: torch.Tensor, mask_ratio: float = 0.1) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Apply cutout augmentation (randomly mask features).
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            mask_ratio: Ratio of features to mask
            
        Returns:
            Masked tensor
        """
        if not self.training or torch.rand(1).item() >= self.augmentation_prob:
            return x
        
        batch_size, num_features = x.shape
        num_mask = int(num_features * mask_ratio)
        
        for i in range(batch_size):
            mask_indices = torch.randperm(num_features)[:num_mask]
            x[i, mask_indices] = 0
        
        return x
    
    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        labels: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        augment_type: str = 'all'
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Optional[torch.Tensor]]:
        """
        Apply preprocessing with augmentation.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            labels: Optional labels
            augment_type: Type of augmentation ('noise', 'dropout', 'mixup', 'cutout', 'all')
            
        Returns:
            Augmented features and labels
        """
        if augment_type in ['noise', 'all']:
            x = self.add_noise(x)
        
        if augment_type in ['dropout', 'all']:
            x = self.feature_dropout_augment(x)
        
        if augment_type in ['cutout', 'all']:
            x = self.cutout(x)
        
        if augment_type in ['mixup', 'all']:
            x, labels = self.mixup(x, labels)
        
        return x, labels

def benchmark_preprocessing_patterns():
    """Benchmark different preprocessing patterns for performance."""
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PREPROCESSING PERFORMANCE BENCHMARK")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    import time
    
    # Test parameters
    batch_size = 128
    num_features = 256
    seq_len = 64
    num_iterations = 100
    
    # Generate test data
    data = torch.randn(batch_size, num_features)
    seq_data = torch.randn(batch_size, seq_len, num_features)
    
    # Benchmark different preprocessing methods
    results = {}
    
    # 1. Feature Scaling
    print("\n1. Feature Scaling Benchmark:")
    scaler = FeatureScaler(num_features=num_features, method='standard')
    scaler.eval()
    
    start_time = time.time()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(num_iterations):
            _ = scaler(data)
    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    results['Feature Scaling'] = elapsed / num_iterations
    print(f"   Average time: {results['Feature Scaling']*1000:.4f} ms")
    
    # 2. Dynamic Preprocessing
    print("\n2. Dynamic Preprocessing Benchmark:")
    dynamic_prep = DynamicPreprocessor(input_dim=num_features)
    dynamic_prep.eval()
    
    start_time = time.time()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(num_iterations):
            _ = dynamic_prep(data)
    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    results['Dynamic Preprocessing'] = elapsed / num_iterations
    print(f"   Average time: {results['Dynamic Preprocessing']*1000:.4f} ms")
    
    # 3. Temporal Preprocessing
    print("\n3. Temporal Preprocessing Benchmark:")
    temporal_prep = TemporalPreprocessor(input_dim=num_features)
    temporal_prep.eval()
    
    start_time = time.time()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(num_iterations):
            _ = temporal_prep(seq_data)
    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    results['Temporal Preprocessing'] = elapsed / num_iterations
    print(f"   Average time: {results['Temporal Preprocessing']*1000:.4f} ms")
    
    # 4. Hierarchical Preprocessing
    print("\n4. Hierarchical Preprocessing Benchmark:")
    hier_prep = HierarchicalPreprocessor(input_dim=num_features, num_levels=3)
    hier_prep.eval()
    
    start_time = time.time()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(num_iterations):
            _ = hier_prep(data)
    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    results['Hierarchical Preprocessing'] = elapsed / num_iterations
    print(f"   Average time: {results['Hierarchical Preprocessing']*1000:.4f} ms")
    
    # Summary
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("BENCHMARK SUMMARY:")
    print("-" * 80)
    fastest = min(results.values())
    for method, time_ms in sorted(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]):
        speedup = fastest / time_ms
        print(f"{method:30s}: {time_ms*1000:8.4f} ms (speedup: {speedup:.2f}x)")

    print("=" * 80)
    print("""
PITFALL 1: Data Leakage
   Problem: Fitting preprocessors on entire dataset including test data
   Solution: Always fit on training data only, transform test data

PITFALL 2: Inconsistent Preprocessing
   Problem: Different preprocessing between training and inference
   Solution: Save preprocessor state, use same pipeline for both

PITFALL 3: Memory Issues with Large Vocabularies
   Problem: One-hot encoding creates huge sparse matrices
   Solution: Use embeddings instead of one-hot for high cardinality

PITFALL 4: Ignoring Padding in Computations
   Problem: Including padding tokens in loss/metrics calculations
   Solution: Always use attention masks to exclude padding

PITFALL 5: Not Handling Unknown Tokens
   Problem: Encountering tokens not in vocabulary at inference
   Solution: Always include UNK token and handle gracefully

PITFALL 6: Forgetting to Update Running Statistics
   Problem: Using stale statistics for normalization
   Solution: Ensure statistics update during training mode

PITFALL 7: Incorrect Batching of Variable-Length Sequences
   Problem: Inefficient or incorrect padding strategies
   Solution: Use dynamic batching with proper collation

PITFALL 8: Not Validating Preprocessed Data
   Problem: Silent preprocessing errors propagating through pipeline
   Solution: Add assertions and validation checks
    """)
