def advanced_techniques():
    """Demonstrate advanced techniques and optimizations."""
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("ADVANCED TECHNIQUES & OPTIMIZATIONS")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # 1. NFE Regularization
    print("\n1. NFE (Number of Function Evaluations) Regularization")
    print("-" * 70)
    print("""
    Control computational cost by penalizing excessive function evaluations:
    
    class NFERegularizedODE(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, func, nfe_weight=0.01):
            super().__init__()
            self.func = func
            self.nfe_weight = nfe_weight
        
        def forward(self, x):
            self.func.nfe = 0
            out = odeint_adjoint(self.func, x, t)
            # Add NFE penalty to loss
            nfe_penalty = self.nfe_weight * self.func.nfe
            return out, nfe_penalty
    
    Benefits:
      • Faster inference
      • More efficient models
      • Controllable speed/accuracy tradeoff
    """)
    
    # 2. Time-dependent parameters
    print("\n2. Time-Dependent Network Parameters")
    print("-" * 70)

    Incorporate time explicitly into the network:
    
    class TimeDepODEFunc(nn.Module):
        def forward(self, t, x):
            # Concatenate time as input feature
            t_vec = t.expand(x.shape[0], 1)
            tx = torch.cat([x, t_vec], dim=1)
            return self.net(tx)
    
    Or use time-dependent weights:
    
    class HyperODEFunc(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
            self.hyper_net = nn.Linear(1, hidden_dim * dim)
        
        def forward(self, t, x):
            # Generate weights based on time
            weights = self.hyper_net(t.view(1, 1))
            # Use weights to transform x
            ...
    
    Benefits:
      • More expressive dynamics
      • Better handling of time-varying systems
    """)
    
    # 3. Multiple timescales
    print("\n3. Multiple Timescale Integration")
    print("-" * 70)
    print("""
    Handle systems with different timescales:
    
    class MultiScaleODE(nn.Module):
        def forward(self, x):
            # Fast dynamics (t=0 to t=0.1)
            t_fast = torch.tensor([0., 0.1])
            x = odeint(self.fast_func, x, t_fast)[-1]
            
            # Slow dynamics (t=0 to t=1)
            t_slow = torch.tensor([0., 1.0])
            x = odeint(self.slow_func, x, t_slow)[-1]
            
            return x
    
    Applications:
      • Climate modeling
      • Chemical reactions
      • Multi-physics simulations
    """)
    
    # 4. Symplectic integration
    print("\n4. Symplectic Integration for Hamiltonian Systems")
    print("-" * 70)
    print("""
    Preserve physical properties (energy, volume) using symplectic methods:
    
    class SymplecticODE(nn.Module):
        def forward(self, qp):
            # Split into position (q) and momentum (p)
            q, p = qp.chunk(2, dim=1)
            
            # Symplectic Euler step
            p_new = p - dt * grad_V(q)  # Update momentum
            q_new = q + dt * p_new / m   # Update position
            
            return torch.cat([q_new, p_new], dim=1)
    
    Properties:
      • Energy conservation
      • Long-term stability
      • Physically consistent
    """)
    
    # 5. Adaptive depth
    print("\n5. Adaptive Depth Control")
    print("-" * 70)
    print("""
    Dynamically adjust integration time based on input:
    
    class AdaptiveDepthODE(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
            self.depth_predictor = nn.Linear(dim, 1)
        
        def forward(self, x):
            # Predict integration time
            T = torch.sigmoid(self.depth_predictor(x)) + 0.5
            
            # Integrate to predicted time
            for i in range(x.shape[0]):
                t = torch.tensor([0., T[i].item()])
                x[i] = odeint(self.func, x[i:i+1], t)[-1]
            
            return x
    
    Benefits:
      • Input-dependent computation
      • Better efficiency
      • Adaptive capacity
    """)

```python
"""
Feature Visualization Pattern
Visualizes what patterns in the input maximize the activation of specific neurons or layers.
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
from torchvision import models, transforms
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


class FeatureVisualizer:
    """
    Implements feature visualization to understand what activates specific neurons.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model, target_layer, device='cuda'):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained neural network
            target_layer: Layer to visualize
            device: Computing device
        """
        self.model = model.to(device)
        self.device = device
        self.target_layer = target_layer
        self.activations = None
        
        # Register hook to capture activations
        self._register_hooks()
        
    def _register_hooks(self):
        """Register forward hook to capture layer activations."""
        def hook_fn(module, input, output):
            self.activations = output
            
        # Find and attach hook to target layer
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if name == self.target_layer:
                module.register_forward_hook(hook_fn)
                
    def visualize_filter(self, filter_index, iterations=30, lr=0.1, 
                        img_size=224, regularization_weight=1e-4):
        """
        Generate an image that maximally activates a specific filter.
        
        Args:
            filter_index: Index of the filter to visualize
            iterations: Number of optimization iterations
            lr: Learning rate
            img_size: Size of generated image
            regularization_weight: Weight for regularization
            
        Returns:
            Generated image as numpy array
        """
        # Initialize random image
        img = torch.randn(1, 3, img_size, img_size, device=self.device)
        img.requires_grad_(True)
        
        optimizer = optim.Adam([img], lr=lr)
        
        self.model.eval()
        
        for i in range(iterations):
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            
            # Forward pass
            _ = self.model(img)
            
            # Get activation of target filter
            if len(self.activations.shape) == 4:  # Conv layer
                loss = -self.activations[0, filter_index].mean()
            else:  # FC layer
                loss = -self.activations[0, filter_index]
            
            # Add regularization (L2 norm) to prevent extreme values
            reg_loss = regularization_weight * torch.norm(img)
            total_loss = loss + reg_loss
            
            # Backward pass
            total_loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            # Clip values to valid range
            with torch.no_grad():
                img.clamp_(-2, 2)
            
            if (i + 1) % 10 == 0:
                print(f"Iteration {i+1}/{iterations}, Loss: {loss.item():.4f}")
        
        # Convert to displayable image
        result = self._postprocess_image(img)
        return result
    
    def _postprocess_image(self, img_tensor):
        """Convert tensor to displayable numpy array."""
        img = img_tensor.detach().cpu().squeeze().numpy()
        img = np.transpose(img, (1, 2, 0))
        
        # Normalize to [0, 1]
        img = (img - img.min()) / (img.max() - img.min())
        return img
    
    def visualize_multiple_filters(self, num_filters=16, **kwargs):
        """Visualize multiple filters in a grid."""
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 4, figsize=(12, 12))
        axes = axes.flatten()
        
        for i in range(num_filters):
            img = self.visualize_filter(i, **kwargs)
            axes[i].imshow(img)
            axes[i].set_title(f'Filter {i}')
            axes[i].axis('off')
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        return fig


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Load pre-trained VGG16
    model = models.vgg16(pretrained=True)
    
    # Visualize filters from conv layer
    visualizer = FeatureVisualizer(
        model=model.features,  # Use only conv layers
        target_layer='10',  # Layer index
        device='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    )
    
    # Visualize a single filter
    img = visualizer.visualize_filter(filter_index=0, iterations=30)
    plt.imshow(img)
    plt.title('Maximally Activating Pattern for Filter 0')
    plt.axis('off')
    plt.savefig('feature_visualization.png')
    plt.show()

## 2. DeepDream Pattern

```python
"""
DeepDream Pattern
Creates dream-like hallucinogenic images by amplifying patterns detected by a neural network.
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torchvision import models, transforms
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np


class DeepDream:
    """
    Implements the DeepDream algorithm for generating surreal images.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model, device='cuda'):
        """
        Args:
            model: Pre-trained neural network
            device: Computing device
        """
        self.model = model.to(device)
        self.device = device
        self.model.eval()
        
        # Normalization used during training
        self.normalize = transforms.Normalize(
            mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406],
            std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225]
        )
        
    def dream(self, image, layers, iterations=20, lr=0.01, octave_scale=1.4, 
              num_octaves=4):
        """
        Apply DeepDream to an image.
        
        Args:
            image: Input PIL Image
            layers: List of layer names to maximize
            iterations: Number of gradient ascent steps
            lr: Learning rate
            octave_scale: Scale factor between octaves
            num_octaves: Number of octaves to process
            
        Returns:
            Dreamed PIL Image
        """
        # Convert to tensor
        img = self._preprocess_image(image)
        
        # Generate octave images (different scales)
        octaves = self._generate_octaves(img, num_octaves, octave_scale)
        
        # Process each octave
        detail = torch.zeros_like(octaves[-1])
        
        for octave_idx, octave_base in enumerate(octaves[::-1]):
            if octave_idx > 0:
                # Upsample detail to current octave size
                detail = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(
                    detail,
                    size=octave_base.shape[2:],
                    mode='bilinear',
                    align_corners=True
                )
            
            # Add detail from previous octave
            input_img = octave_base + detail
            
            # Optimize this octave
            dreamed = self._optimize_octave(input_img, layers, iterations, lr)
            
            # Extract detail for next octave
            detail = dreamed - octave_base
            
            print(f"Processed octave {octave_idx + 1}/{num_octaves}")
        
        # Convert back to PIL Image
        result = self._postprocess_image(dreamed)
        return result
    
    def _generate_octaves(self, img, num_octaves, octave_scale):
        """Generate images at different scales."""
        octaves = [img]
        
        for _ in range(num_octaves - 1):
            # Downscale image
            new_size = (
                int(octaves[-1].shape[2] / octave_scale),
                int(octaves[-1].shape[3] / octave_scale)
            )
            downscaled = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(
                octaves[-1],
                size=new_size,
                mode='bilinear',
                align_corners=True
            )
            octaves.append(downscaled)
        
        return octaves
    
    def _optimize_octave(self, img, layers, iterations, lr):
        """Perform gradient ascent on one octave."""
        img = img.clone().requires_grad_(True)
        
        # Register hooks for target layers
        activations = {}
        hooks = []
        
        def get_activation(name):
            def hook(module, input, output):
                activations[name] = output
            return hook
        
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if name in layers:
                hooks.append(module.register_forward_hook(get_activation(name)))
        
        for i in range(iterations):
            # Zero gradients
            if img.grad is not None:
                img.grad.zero_()
            
            # Forward pass
            self.model(self.normalize(img))
            
            # Calculate loss (negative to maximize)
            loss = sum([act.norm() for act in activations.values()])
            
            # Backward pass
            loss.backward()
            
            # Gradient ascent
            with torch.no_grad():
                img += lr * img.grad / (torch.abs(img.grad).mean() + 1e-8)
                img.clamp_(0, 1)
        
        # Remove hooks
        for hook in hooks:
            hook.remove()
        
        return img.detach()
    
    def _preprocess_image(self, image):
        """Convert PIL Image to tensor."""
        transform = transforms.Compose([
            transforms.ToTensor(),
        ])
        img_tensor = transform(image).unsqueeze(0).to(self.device)
        return img_tensor
    
    def _postprocess_image(self, img_tensor):
        """Convert tensor to PIL Image."""
        img = img_tensor.squeeze().cpu().clamp(0, 1)
        img = transforms.ToPILImage()(img)
        return img


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Load pre-trained model
    model = models.vgg16(pretrained=True).features
    
    # Create DeepDream instance
    dreamer = DeepDream(
        model=model,
        device='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    )
    
    # Load input image
    input_image = Image.open('input.jpg').resize((512, 512))
    
    # Apply DeepDream
    # Target layers from VGG16
    target_layers = ['17', '24', '28']  # Conv layers
    
    dreamed_image = dreamer.dream(
        image=input_image,
        layers=target_layers,
        iterations=20,
        num_octaves=4
    )
    
    dreamed_image.save('deepdream_output.jpg')
    print("DeepDream complete!")
```

"""
Neural Style Transfer Pattern
Transfers the artistic style from one image to another while preserving content.
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
from torchvision import models, transforms
from PIL import Image
import copy


class NeuralStyleTransfer:
    """
    Implements neural style transfer using the Gatys et al. method.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, device='cuda'):
        """
        Args:
            device: Computing device
        """
        self.device = device
        
        # Load pre-trained VGG19
        vgg = models.vgg19(pretrained=True).features.to(device).eval()
        self.model = vgg
        
        # Freeze all parameters
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad_(False)
        
        # Normalization for VGG
        self.normalize = transforms.Normalize(
            mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406],
            std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225]
        )
        
        # Layers for content and style
        self.content_layers = ['conv_4']
        self.style_layers = ['conv_1', 'conv_2', 'conv_3', 'conv_4', 'conv_5']
        
    def transfer_style(self, content_img, style_img, num_steps=300,
                       style_weight=1000000, content_weight=1,
                       learning_rate=0.003):
        """
        Perform neural style transfer.
        
        Args:
            content_img: PIL Image for content
            style_img: PIL Image for style
            num_steps: Number of optimization steps
            style_weight: Weight for style loss
            content_weight: Weight for content loss
            learning_rate: Learning rate for optimizer
            
        Returns:
            Stylized PIL Image
        """
        # Preprocess images
        content_tensor = self._preprocess_image(content_img)
        style_tensor = self._preprocess_image(style_img)
        
        # Initialize output image (start from content image)
        output_img = content_tensor.clone().requires_grad_(True)
        
        # Extract features
        content_features = self._extract_features(content_tensor)
        style_features = self._extract_features(style_tensor)
        
        # Calculate style gram matrices
        style_grams = {
            layer: self._gram_matrix(style_features[layer])
            for layer in self.style_layers
        }
        
        # Optimizer
        optimizer = optim.LBFGS([output_img], lr=learning_rate)
        
        run = [0]
        
        def closure():
            """Optimization closure function."""
            # Clamp output image
            with torch.no_grad():
                output_img.clamp_(0, 1)
            
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            
            # Extract features from output
            output_features = self._extract_features(output_img)
            
            # Content loss
            content_loss = 0
            for layer in self.content_layers:
                content_loss += torch.mean(
                    (output_features[layer] - content_features[layer]) ** 2
                )
            content_loss *= content_weight
            
            # Style loss
            style_loss = 0
            for layer in self.style_layers:
                output_gram = self._gram_matrix(output_features[layer])
                style_gram = style_grams[layer]
                layer_loss = torch.mean((output_gram - style_gram) ** 2)
                style_loss += layer_loss / len(self.style_layers)
            style_loss *= style_weight
            
            # Total loss
            total_loss = content_loss + style_loss
            total_loss.backward()
            
            run[0] += 1
            if run[0] % 50 == 0:
                print(f"Step {run[0]}/{num_steps}")
                print(f"  Content Loss: {content_loss.item():.4f}")
                print(f"  Style Loss: {style_loss.item():.4f}")
                print(f"  Total Loss: {total_loss.item():.4f}")
            
            return total_loss
        
        # Optimize
        for step in range(num_steps):
            optimizer.step(closure)
        
        # Final clamp
        with torch.no_grad():
            output_img.clamp_(0, 1
```python
        # Final clamp
        with torch.no_grad():
            output_img.clamp_(0, 1)
        
        # Convert to PIL Image
        result = self._postprocess_image(output_img)
        return result
    
    def _extract_features(self, image):
        """Extract features from specified layers."""
        features = {}
        x = image
        
        # VGG19 layer mapping
        layer_names = {
            '0': 'conv_1',
            '5': 'conv_2',
            '10': 'conv_3',
            '19': 'conv_4',
            '28': 'conv_5'
        }
        
        for name, layer in self.model._modules.items():
            x = layer(x)
            if name in layer_names:
                features[layer_names[name]] = x
        
        return features
    
    def _gram_matrix(self, tensor):
        """
        Calculate Gram matrix for style representation.
        
        Args:
            tensor: Feature map tensor (batch, channels, height, width)
            
        Returns:
            Gram matrix
        """
        batch, channels, height, width = tensor.size()
        
        # Reshape to (channels, height*width)
        features = tensor.view(batch * channels, height * width)
        
        # Calculate gram matrix
        gram = torch.mm(features, features.t())
        
        # Normalize by number of elements
        return gram.div(batch * channels * height * width)
    
    def _preprocess_image(self, image, max_size=512):
        """Convert PIL Image to tensor."""
        # Resize if too large
        if max(image.size) > max_size:
            size = max_size
        else:
            size = max(image.size)
        
        transform = transforms.Compose([
            transforms.Resize(size),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
        ])
        
        img_tensor = transform(image).unsqueeze(0).to(self.device)
        return img_tensor
    
    def _postprocess_image(self, img_tensor):
        """Convert tensor to PIL Image."""
        img = img_tensor.squeeze().cpu().clamp(0, 1)
        img = transforms.ToPILImage()(img)
        return img

"""
Texture Synthesis Pattern
Generates new textures from example textures using neural networks.
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
from torchvision import models, transforms
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np


class TextureSynthesizer:
    """
    Synthesizes textures using neural network feature statistics.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, device='cuda'):
        """
        Args:
            device: Computing device
        """
        self.device = device
        
        # Load pre-trained VGG19
        vgg = models.vgg19(pretrained=True).features.to(device).eval()
        self.model = vgg
        
        # Freeze parameters
        for param in self.model.parameters():
            param.requires_grad_(False)
        
        # Layers to use for texture synthesis
        self.texture_layers = ['conv_1', 'conv_2', 'conv_3', 'conv_4', 'conv_5']
        
    def synthesize(self, texture_img, output_size=(512, 512), 
                   num_steps=500, learning_rate=0.01):
        """
        Synthesize a new texture from an example.
        
        Args:
            texture_img: PIL Image of example texture
            output_size: Size of output texture (height, width)
            num_steps: Number of optimization steps
            learning_rate: Learning rate
            
        Returns:
            Synthesized texture as PIL Image
        """
        # Preprocess texture image
        texture_tensor = self._preprocess_image(texture_img)
        
        # Extract texture features and compute gram matrices
        texture_features = self._extract_features(texture_tensor)
        texture_grams = {
            layer: self._gram_matrix(texture_features[layer])
            for layer in self.texture_layers
        }
        
        # Initialize output with random noise
        output_img = torch.randn(
            1, 3, output_size[0], output_size[1],
            device=self.device,
            requires_grad=True
        )
        
        # Optimizer
        optimizer = optim.LBFGS([output_img], lr=learning_rate)
        
        run = [0]
        
        def closure():
            """Optimization closure."""
            # Clamp to valid range
            with torch.no_grad():
                output_img.clamp_(0, 1)
            
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            
            # Extract features from current output
            output_features = self._extract_features(output_img)
            
            # Calculate texture loss (gram matrix differences)
            total_loss = 0
            layer_losses = {}
            
            for layer in self.texture_layers:
                output_gram = self._gram_matrix(output_features[layer])
                texture_gram = texture_grams[layer]
                
                layer_loss = torch.mean((output_gram - texture_gram) ** 2)
                layer_losses[layer] = layer_loss.item()
                total_loss += layer_loss
            
            total_loss.backward()
            
            run[0] += 1
            if run[0] % 50 == 0:
                print(f"Step {run[0]}/{num_steps}, Loss: {total_loss.item():.4f}")
                for layer, loss in layer_losses.items():
                    print(f"  {layer}: {loss:.4f}")
            
            return total_loss
        
        # Optimize
        for step in range(num_steps):
            optimizer.step(closure)
        
        # Final clamp
        with torch.no_grad():
            output_img.clamp_(0, 1)
        
        # Convert to PIL Image
        result = self._postprocess_image(output_img)
        return result
    
    def synthesize_with_histogram_matching(self, texture_img, output_size=(512, 512),
                                          num_steps=500, learning_rate=0.01):
        """
        Synthesize texture with histogram matching for color preservation.
        
        Args:
            texture_img: PIL Image of example texture
            output_size: Size of output texture
            num_steps: Number of optimization steps
            learning_rate: Learning rate
            
        Returns:
            Synthesized texture with matched histogram
        """
        # First, synthesize texture
        synthesized = self.synthesize(
            texture_img, output_size, num_steps, learning_rate
        )
        
        # Match histogram to original texture
        matched = self._match_histogram(synthesized, texture_img)
        return matched
    
    def _extract_features(self, image):
        """Extract features from specified layers."""
        features = {}
        x = image
        
        layer_names = {
            '0': 'conv_1',
            '5': 'conv_2',
            '10': 'conv_3',
            '19': 'conv_4',
            '28': 'conv_5'
        }
        
        for name, layer in self.model._modules.items():
            x = layer(x)
            if name in layer_names:
                features[layer_names[name]] = x
        
        return features
    
    def _gram_matrix(self, tensor):
        """Calculate Gram matrix."""
        batch, channels, height, width = tensor.size()
        features = tensor.view(batch * channels, height * width)
        gram = torch.mm(features, features.t())
        return gram.div(batch * channels * height * width)
    
    def _match_histogram(self, source_img, reference_img):
        """Match histogram of source to reference."""
        source_array = np.array(source_img)
        reference_array = np.array(reference_img)
        
        matched = np.zeros_like(source_array)
        
        for channel in range(3):
            source_channel = source_array[:, :, channel].flatten()
            reference_channel = reference_array[:, :, channel].flatten()
            
            # Sort pixel values
            source_sorted = np.sort(source_channel)
            reference_sorted = np.sort(reference_channel)
            
            # Create mapping
            indices = np.searchsorted(source_sorted, source_channel)
            indices = np.clip(indices, 0, len(reference_sorted) - 1)
            
            matched[:, :, channel] = reference_sorted[indices].reshape(
                source_array.shape[:2]
            )
        
        return Image.fromarray(matched.astype(np.uint8))
    
    def _preprocess_image(self, image):
        """Convert PIL Image to tensor."""
        transform = transforms.Compose([
            transforms.ToTensor(),
        ])
        img_tensor = transform(image).unsqueeze(0).to(self.device)
        return img_tensor
    
    def _postprocess_image(self, img_tensor):
        """Convert tensor to PIL Image."""
        img = img_tensor.squeeze().cpu().clamp(0, 1)
        img = transforms.ToPILImage()(img)
        return img


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Create synthesizer
    synthesizer = TextureSynthesizer(
        device='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    )
    
    # Load texture image
    texture_image = Image.open('texture.jpg')
    
    # Synthesize new texture
    synthesized_texture = synthesizer.synthesize(
        texture_img=texture_image,
        output_size=(512, 512),
        num_steps=500
    )
    
    synthesized_texture.save('synthesized_texture.jpg')
    
    # Synthesize with histogram matching
    matched_texture = synthesizer.synthesize_with_histogram_matching(
        texture_img=texture_image,
        output_size=(512, 512),
        num_steps=500
    )
    
    matched_texture.save('matched_texture.jpg')
    print("Texture synthesis complete!")

## 5. Adversarial Example Generation Pattern

```python
"""
Adversarial Example Generation Pattern
Generates adversarial examples that fool neural networks.
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torchvision import models, transforms
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np


class AdversarialExampleGenerator:
    """
    Generates adversarial examples using various attack methods.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model, device='cuda'):
        """
        Args:
            model: Target neural network to attack
            device: Computing device
        """
        self.model = model.to(device)
        self.device = device
        self.model.eval()
        
        # Standard ImageNet normalization
        self.normalize = transforms.Normalize(
            mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406],
            std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225]
        )
        
    def fgsm_attack(self, image, target_class, epsilon=0.03):
        """
        Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) attack.
        
        Args:
            image: Input PIL Image
            target_class: Target class for misclassification
            epsilon: Perturbation magnitude
            
        Returns:
            Adversarial image as PIL Image
        """
        # Preprocess image
        img_tensor = self._preprocess_image(image)
        img_tensor.requires_grad_(True)
        
        # Forward pass
        output = self.model(self.normalize(img_tensor))
        
        # Calculate loss
        loss = F.cross_entropy(output, torch.tensor([target_class]).to(self.device))
        
        # Backward pass
        self.model.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        
        # Generate adversarial example
        with torch.no_grad():
            # Get sign of gradient
            sign_gradient = img_tensor.grad.sign()
            
            # Add perturbation
            adversarial = img_tensor + epsilon * sign_gradient
            
            # Clamp to valid range
            adversarial = torch.clamp(adversarial, 0, 1)
        
        # Convert to PIL Image
        result = self._postprocess_image(adversarial)
        return result
    
    def iterative_fgsm_attack(self, image, target_class, epsilon=0.03,
                             alpha=0.01, num_iterations=10):
        """
        Iterative FGSM (I-FGSM) attack, also known as Basic Iterative Method.
        
        Args:
            image: Input PIL Image
            target_class: Target class
            epsilon: Maximum perturbation
            alpha: Step size per iteration
            num_iterations: Number of iterations
            
        Returns:
            Adversarial image as PIL Image
        """
        # Preprocess image
        original_img = self._preprocess_image(image)
        adversarial = original_img.clone()
        
        for i in range(num_iterations):
            adversarial.requires_grad_(True)
            
            # Forward pass
            output = self.model(self.normalize(adversarial))
            
            # Calculate loss
            loss = F.cross_entropy(
                output,
                torch.tensor([target_class]).to(self.device)
            )
            
            # Backward pass
            self.model.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            
            # Update adversarial example
            with torch.no_grad():
                sign_gradient = adversarial.grad.sign()
                adversarial = adversarial + alpha * sign_gradient
                
                # Project back to epsilon ball around original
                perturbation = torch.clamp(
                    adversarial - original_img,
                    -epsilon,
                    epsilon
                )
                adversarial = torch.clamp(original_img + perturbation, 0, 1)
            
            if (i + 1) % 5 == 0:
                pred = output.argmax(dim=1).item()
                print(f"Iteration {i+1}/{num_iterations}, Predicted: {pred}")
        
        # Convert to PIL Image
        result = self._postprocess_image(adversarial)
        return result
    
    def pgd_attack(self, image, target_class, epsilon=0.03, alpha=0.01,
                   num_iterations=40, random_start=True):
        """
        Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) attack.
        
        Args:
            image: Input PIL Image
            target_class: Target class
            epsilon: Maximum perturbation
            alpha: Step size
            num_iterations: Number of iterations
            random_start: Whether to start from random point in epsilon ball
            
        Returns:
            Adversarial image as PIL Image
        """
        # Preprocess image
        original_img = self
```python
        # Preprocess image
        original_img = self._preprocess_image(image)
        
        # Initialize adversarial example
        if random_start:
            # Start from random point in epsilon ball
            adversarial = original_img + torch.empty_like(original_img).uniform_(
                -epsilon, epsilon
            )
            adversarial = torch.clamp(adversarial, 0, 1)
        else:
            adversarial = original_img.clone()
        
        for i in range(num_iterations):
            adversarial.requires_grad_(True)
            
            # Forward pass
            output = self.model(self.normalize(adversarial))
            
            # Calculate loss (negative for targeted attack)
            loss = -F.cross_entropy(
                output,
                torch.tensor([target_class]).to(self.device)
            )
            
            # Backward pass
            self.model.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            
            # Update adversarial example
            with torch.no_grad():
                # Gradient descent step
                adversarial = adversarial + alpha * adversarial.grad.sign()
                
                # Project onto epsilon ball
                perturbation = torch.clamp(
                    adversarial - original_img,
                    -epsilon,
                    epsilon
                )
                adversarial = torch.clamp(original_img + perturbation, 0, 1)
            
            if (i + 1) % 10 == 0:
                pred = output.argmax(dim=1).item()
                conf = F.softmax(output, dim=1)[0, pred].item()
                print(f"Iteration {i+1}/{num_iterations}, "
                      f"Predicted: {pred}, Confidence: {conf:.4f}")
        
        # Convert to PIL Image
        result = self._postprocess_image(adversarial)
        return result
    
    def carlini_wagner_attack(self, image, target_class, c=1.0, kappa=0,
                             num_iterations=1000, learning_rate=0.01):
        """
        Carlini & Wagner (C&W) L2 attack.
        
        Args:
            image: Input PIL Image
            target_class: Target class
            c: Constant balancing perturbation and loss
            kappa: Confidence parameter
            num_iterations: Number of optimization iterations
            learning_rate: Learning rate
            
        Returns:
            Adversarial image as PIL Image
        """
        # Preprocess image
        original_img = self._preprocess_image(image)
        
        # Initialize perturbation in tanh space for box constraints
        w = torch.zeros_like(original_img, requires_grad=True)
        
        # Optimizer
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam([w], lr=learning_rate)
        
        best_adversarial = None
        best_l2 = float('inf')
        
        for i in range(num_iterations):
            # Convert w to image space using tanh
            adversarial = 0.5 * (torch.tanh(w) + 1)
            
            # Forward pass
            output = self.model(self.normalize(adversarial))
            
            # Calculate L2 distance
            l2_dist = torch.norm(adversarial - original_img)
            
            # Calculate classification loss
            # f(x) = max(max{Z(x)_i : i != t} - Z(x)_t, -kappa)
            logits = output[0]
            target_logit = logits[target_class]
            
            # Get maximum logit for non-target classes
            other_logits = torch.cat([
                logits[:target_class],
                logits[target_class + 1:]
            ])
            max_other_logit = torch.max(other_logits)
            
            # f(x) for targeted attack
            f = torch.clamp(max_other_logit - target_logit, min=-kappa)
            
            # Total loss
            loss = l2_dist + c * f
            
            # Backward pass
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            # Track best adversarial example
            with torch.no_grad():
                if f <= 0 and l2_dist < best_l2:
                    best_l2 = l2_dist.item()
                    best_adversarial = adversarial.clone()
            
            if (i + 1) % 100 == 0:
                pred = output.argmax(dim=1).item()
                print(f"Iteration {i+1}/{num_iterations}, "
                      f"L2: {l2_dist.item():.4f}, "
                      f"f(x): {f.item():.4f}, "
                      f"Predicted: {pred}")
        
        # Use best adversarial example if found, otherwise use final
        if best_adversarial is not None:
            result_tensor = best_adversarial
        else:
            result_tensor = 0.5 * (torch.tanh(w) + 1)
        
        # Convert to PIL Image
        result = self._postprocess_image(result_tensor)
        return result
    
    def deepfool_attack(self, image, num_classes=10, max_iterations=50,
                       overshoot=0.02):
        """
        DeepFool attack - finds minimal perturbation to cross decision boundary.
        
        Args:
            image: Input PIL Image
            num_classes: Number of classes to consider
            max_iterations: Maximum iterations
            overshoot: Overshoot parameter
            
        Returns:
            Adversarial image as PIL Image
        """
        # Preprocess image
        original_img = self._preprocess_image(image)
        adversarial = original_img.clone()
        
        # Get original prediction
        with torch.no_grad():
            output = self.model(self.normalize(original_img))
            original_class = output.argmax(dim=1).item()
        
        current_class = original_class
        iteration = 0
        
        while current_class == original_class and iteration < max_iterations:
            adversarial.requires_grad_(True)
            
            # Forward pass
            output = self.model(self.normalize(adversarial))
            
            # Get top k classes
            _, top_classes = output.topk(min(num_classes, output.size(1)))
            top_classes = top_classes[0]
            
            # Calculate gradients for each class
            gradients = []
            values = []
            
            for k in top_classes:
                if k == original_class:
                    continue
                
                self.model.zero_grad()
                if adversarial.grad is not None:
                    adversarial.grad.zero_()
                
                # Get gradient of k-th class score
                output[0, k].backward(retain_graph=True)
                grad_k = adversarial.grad.clone()
                
                # Get gradient of original class score
                self.model.zero_grad()
                adversarial.grad.zero_()
                output[0, original_class].backward(retain_graph=True)
                grad_orig = adversarial.grad.clone()
                
                # Relative gradient
                w = grad_k - grad_orig
                f = output[0, k] - output[0, original_class]
                
                gradients.append(w)
                values.append(f.item())
            
            # Find minimal perturbation
            with torch.no_grad():
                min_distance = float('inf')
                min_perturbation = None
                
                for w, f in zip(gradients, values):
                    distance = abs(f) / (torch.norm(w.flatten()) + 1e-8)
                    
                    if distance < min_distance:
                        min_distance = distance
                        min_perturbation = (f / (torch.norm(w.flatten()) ** 2 + 1e-8)) * w
                
                # Add perturbation with overshoot
                if min_perturbation is not None:
                    adversarial = adversarial + (1 + overshoot) * min_perturbation
                    adversarial = torch.clamp(adversarial, 0, 1)
            
            # Check current prediction
            with torch.no_grad():
                output = self.model(self.normalize(adversarial))
                current_class = output.argmax(dim=1).item()
            
            iteration += 1
            
            if iteration % 10 == 0:
                print(f"Iteration {iteration}, Current class: {current_class}")
        
        print(f"DeepFool converged in {iteration} iterations")
        print(f"Original class: {original_class}, Final class: {current_class}")
        
        # Convert to PIL Image
        result = self._postprocess_image(adversarial)
        return result
    
    def evaluate_attack(self, original_img, adversarial_img, true_class):
        """
        Evaluate the success of an adversarial attack.
        
        Args:
            original_img: Original PIL Image
            adversarial_img: Adversarial PIL Image
            true_class: True class label
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with evaluation metrics
        """
        # Preprocess images
        original_tensor = self._preprocess_image(original_img)
        adversarial_tensor = self._preprocess_image(adversarial_img)
        
        # Get predictions
        with torch.no_grad():
            original_output = self.model(self.normalize(original_tensor))
            adversarial_output = self.model(self.normalize(adversarial_tensor))
            
            original_pred = original_output.argmax(dim=1).item()
            adversarial_pred = adversarial_output.argmax(dim=1).item()
            
            original_conf = F.softmax(original_output, dim=1)[0, original_pred].item()
            adversarial_conf = F.softmax(adversarial_output, dim=1)[0, adversarial_pred].item()
        
        # Calculate perturbation metrics
        perturbation = (adversarial_tensor - original_tensor).squeeze()
        l2_norm = torch.norm(perturbation).item()
        linf_norm = torch.max(torch.abs(perturbation)).item()
        
        # Calculate PSNR
        mse = torch.mean((adversarial_tensor - original_tensor) ** 2).item()
        psnr = 10 * np.log10(1.0 / (mse + 1e-10))
        
        results = {
            'original_prediction': original_pred,
            'adversarial_prediction': adversarial_pred,
            'original_confidence': original_conf,
            'adversarial_confidence': adversarial_conf,
            'attack_success': original_pred != adversarial_pred,
            'l2_norm': l2_norm,
            'linf_norm': linf_norm,
            'psnr': psnr
        }
        
        return results
    
    def _preprocess_image(self, image):
        """Convert PIL Image to tensor."""
        transform = transforms.Compose([
            transforms.Resize(224),
            transforms.CenterCrop(224),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
        ])
        img_tensor = transform(image).unsqueeze(0).to(self.device)
        return img_tensor
    
    def _postprocess_image(self, img_tensor):
        """Convert tensor to PIL Image."""
        img = img_tensor.squeeze().cpu().clamp(0, 1)
        img = transforms.ToPILImage()(img)
        return img


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Load pre-trained model
    model = models.resnet50(pretrained=True)
    
    # Create adversarial generator
    adv_generator = AdversarialExampleGenerator(
        model=model,
        device='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    )
    
    # Load input image
    input_image = Image.open('input.jpg')
    
    # Define target class (e.g., 281 = 'tabby cat' in ImageNet)
    target_class = 281
    
    print("=" * 60)
    print("FGSM Attack")
    print("=" * 60)
    fgsm_adv = adv_generator.fgsm_attack(
        image=input_image,
        target_class=target_class,
        epsilon=0.03
    )
    fgsm_adv.save('fgsm_adversarial.jpg')
    
    # Evaluate FGSM attack
    fgsm_results = adv_generator.evaluate_attack(input_image, fgsm_adv, target_class)
    print(f"FGSM Results: {fgsm_results}")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("I-FGSM Attack")
    print("=" * 60)
    ifgsm_adv = adv_generator.iterative_fgsm_attack(
        image=input_image,
        target_class=target_class,
        epsilon=0.03,
        alpha=0.01,
        num_iterations=10
    )
    ifgsm_adv.save('ifgsm_adversarial.jpg')
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("PGD Attack")
    print("=" * 60)
    pgd_adv = adv_generator.pgd_attack(
        image=input_image,
        target_class=target_class,
        epsilon=0.03,
        alpha=0.01,
        num_iterations=40
    )
    pgd_adv.save('pgd_adversarial.jpg')
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("C&W Attack")
    print("=" * 60)
    cw_adv = adv_generator.carlini_wagner_attack(
        image=input_image,

    print(f"Original prediction: Class {original_class}, Confidence: {original_conf:.4f}")

def create_sample_image(size=224):
    """Create a sample image with gradients and patterns."""
    img = np.zeros((size, size, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    
    # Create gradient background
    for i in range(size):
        for j in range(size):
            img[i, j, 0] = int(255 * i / size)  # Red gradient
            img[i, j, 1] = int(255 * j / size)  # Green gradient
            img[i, j, 2] = int(128 + 127 * np.sin(i * 0.1) * np.cos(j * 0.1))  # Blue pattern
    
    # Add some geometric shapes
    center = size // 2
    radius = size // 4
    
    for i in range(size):
        for j in range(size):
            dist = np.sqrt((i - center)**2 + (j - center)**2)
            if dist < radius:
                img[i, j] = [255, 255, 255]  # White circle
    
    return Image.fromarray(img)


def create_style_image(size=224):
    """Create a sample style image with artistic patterns."""
    img = np.zeros((size, size, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    
    # Create wavy pattern
    for i in range(size):
        for j in range(size):
            wave1 = np.sin(i * 0.1) * np.cos(j * 0.1)
            wave2 = np.sin(i * 0.05 + j * 0.05)
            
            img[i, j, 0] = int(128 + 127 * wave1)
            img[i, j, 1] = int(128 + 127 * wave2)
            img[i, j, 2] = int(128 + 127 * np.sin(wave1 + wave2))
    
    return Image.fromarray(img)


def create_texture_image(size=128):
    """Create a sample texture image."""
    img = np.zeros((size, size, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    
    # Create brick-like texture
    brick_height = 20
    brick_width = 40
    
    for i in range(size):
        for j in range(size):
            row = i // brick_height
            col = j // brick_width
            
            # Offset every other row
            if row % 2 == 1:
                col = (j + brick_width // 2) // brick_width
            
            # Brick color with variation
            base_color = 180 + (row + col) % 40
            
            # Add mortar lines
            if i % brick_height < 2 or j % brick_width < 2:
                img[i, j] = [200, 200, 200]  # Gray mortar
            else:
                img[i, j] = [base_color, base_color - 50, base_color - 80]  # Red brick
    
    return Image.fromarray(img)


# Utility function to compare results
def compare_results(original_img, processed_imgs, titles, save_path='comparison.png'):
    """
    Compare original image with processed versions.
    
    Args:
        original_img: Original PIL Image
        processed_imgs: List of processed PIL Images
        titles: List of titles for each image
        save_path: Path to save comparison
    """
    n_images = len(processed_imgs) + 1
    cols = min(4, n_images)
    rows = (n_images + cols - 1) // cols
    
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, cols, figsize=(4*cols, 4*rows))
    if n_images == 1:
        axes = [axes]
    else:
        axes = axes.flatten() if rows > 1 else axes
    
    # Show original
    axes[0].imshow(original_img)
    axes[0].set_title('Original')
    axes[0].axis('off')
    
    # Show processed images
    for idx, (img, title) in enumerate(zip(processed_imgs, titles), 1):
        axes[idx].imshow(img)
        axes[idx].set_title(title)
        axes[idx].axis('off')
    
    # Hide extra subplots
    for idx in range(n_images, len(axes)):
        axes[idx].axis('off')
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close()
    print(f"Saved comparison: {save_path}")


# Advanced usage example with custom models
class CustomFeatureExtractor(nn.Module):
    """Custom model for feature extraction."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        super(CustomFeatureExtractor, self).__init__()
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 64, 3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2),
            
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Conv2d(128, 128, 3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2),
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.features(x)

## Summary and Usage Guide

```python
"""
USAGE GUIDE FOR ACTIVATION MAXIMIZATION PATTERNS
================================================

1. FEATURE VISUALIZATION
   Purpose: Understand what patterns activate specific neurons
   Use case: Model interpretability, debugging CNNs
   
   Example:
   >>> visualizer = FeatureVisualizer(model, 'layer_name', device)
   >>> img = visualizer.visualize_filter(filter_index=0)

2. DEEPDREAM
   Purpose: Generate artistic, dream-like images
   Use case: Art generation, understanding network perception
   
   Example:
   >>> dreamer = DeepDream(model, device)
   >>> result = dreamer.dream(image, layers=['conv_3', 'conv_4'])

3. NEURAL STYLE TRANSFER
   Purpose: Apply artistic style to images
   Use case: Image stylization, artistic effects
   
   Example
```python
3. NEURAL STYLE TRANSFER
   Purpose: Apply artistic style to images
   Use case: Image stylization, artistic effects
   
   Example:
   >>> style_transfer = NeuralStyleTransfer(device)
   >>> result = style_transfer.transfer_style(content_img, style_img)

4. TEXTURE SYNTHESIS
   Purpose: Generate new textures from examples
   Use case: Texture generation, material design
   
   Example:
   >>> synthesizer = TextureSynthesizer(device)
   >>> texture = synthesizer.synthesize(texture_img, output_size=(512, 512))

5. ADVERSARIAL EXAMPLE GENERATION
   Purpose: Create inputs that fool neural networks
   Use case: Model robustness testing, security research
   
   Example:
   >>> adv_gen = AdversarialExampleGenerator(model, device)
   >>> adv_img = adv_gen.fgsm_attack(image, target_class)

INSTALLATION REQUIREMENTS
=========================
pip install torch torchvision pillow matplotlib numpy

PERFORMANCE TIPS
================
- Use GPU (CUDA) for faster processing
- Reduce iterations for quick prototyping
- Adjust learning rates based on convergence
- Use smaller image sizes for faster experiments

COMMON PARAMETERS
=================
- iterations: More iterations = better quality but slower
- learning_rate: Higher = faster but less stable
- epsilon (adversarial): Larger = more visible perturbation
- style_weight: Higher = stronger style transfer
- num_octaves (DeepDream): More = finer details

TROUBLESHOOTING
===============
- Out of memory: Reduce image size or batch size
- Poor results: Increase iterations or adjust learning rate
- Slow processing: Use GPU, reduce image size
- Gradient explosion: Lower learning rate
"""


# Additional utility functions for batch processing
class BatchProcessor:
    """Process multiple images efficiently."""
    
    def __init__(self, pattern_type, device='cuda'):
        """
        Args:
            pattern_type: Type of pattern ('feature', 'dream', 'style', 'texture', 'adversarial')
            device: Computing device
        """
        self.device = device
        self.pattern_type = pattern_type
        self._init_processor()
    
    def _init_processor(self):
        """Initialize the appropriate processor."""
        if self.pattern_type == 'feature':
            model = models.vgg16(pretrained=True)
            self.processor = FeatureVisualizer(
                model=model.features,
                target_layer='10',
                device=self.device
            )
        elif self.pattern_type == 'dream':
            model = models.vgg16(pretrained=True)
            self.processor = DeepDream(model=model.features, device=self.device)
        elif self.pattern_type == 'style':
            self.processor = NeuralStyleTransfer(device=self.device)
        elif self.pattern_type == 'texture':
            self.processor = TextureSynthesizer(device=self.device)
        elif self.pattern_type == 'adversarial':
            model = models.resnet50(pretrained=True)
            self.processor = AdversarialExampleGenerator(model=model, device=self.device)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown pattern type: {self.pattern_type}")
    
    def process_batch(self, images, **kwargs):
        """
        Process a batch of images.
        
        Args:
            images: List of PIL Images or file paths
            **kwargs: Pattern-specific parameters
            
        Returns:
            List of processed images
        """
        results = []
        
        for idx, img in enumerate(images):
            print(f"\nProcessing image {idx + 1}/{len(images)}...")
            
            # Load image if path is provided
            if isinstance(img, str):
                img = Image.open(img)
            
            # Process based on pattern type
            if self.pattern_type == 'feature':
                result = self.processor.visualize_filter(**kwargs)
            elif self.pattern_type == 'dream':
                result = self.processor.dream(image=img, **kwargs)
            elif self.pattern_type == 'style':
                result = self.processor.transfer_style(content_img=img, **kwargs)
            elif self.pattern_type == 'texture':
                result = self.processor.synthesize(texture_img=img, **kwargs)
            elif self.pattern_type == 'adversarial':
                result = self.processor.fgsm_attack(image=img, **kwargs)
            
            results.append(result)
        
        return results


# Video processing utilities
class VideoProcessor:
    """Process videos frame by frame with activation maximization patterns."""
    
    def __init__(self, pattern_processor, device='cuda'):
        """
        Args:
            pattern_processor: Instance of pattern processor
            device: Computing device
        """
        self.processor = pattern_processor
        self.device = device
    
    def process_video(self, video_path, output_path, frame_skip=1, **kwargs):
        """
        Process video with selected pattern.
        
        Args:
            video_path: Path to input video
            output_path: Path to output video
            frame_skip: Process every nth frame
            **kwargs: Pattern-specific parameters
        """
        try:
            import cv2
        except ImportError:
            raise ImportError("OpenCV required for video processing. Install with: pip install opencv-python")
        
        # Open video
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(video_path)
        fps = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS))
        width = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH))
        height = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT))
        total_frames = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT))
        
        # Video writer
        fourcc = cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*'mp4v')
        out = cv2.VideoWriter(output_path, fourcc, fps, (width, height))
        
        frame_count = 0
        processed_count = 0
        
        print(f"Processing video: {total_frames} frames at {fps} fps")
        
        while cap.isOpened():
            ret, frame = cap.read()
            if not ret:
                break
            
            frame_count += 1
            
            # Process every nth frame
            if frame_count % frame_skip == 0:
                # Convert BGR to RGB
                frame_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
                pil_img = Image.fromarray(frame_rgb)
                
                # Process frame
                if isinstance(self.processor, DeepDream):
                    processed = self.processor.dream(image=pil_img, **kwargs)
                elif isinstance(self.processor, NeuralStyleTransfer):
                    processed = self.processor.transfer_style(content_img=pil_img, **kwargs)
                else:
                    processed = pil_img  # Fallback
                
                # Convert back to BGR
                processed_array = np.array(processed)
                processed_bgr = cv2.cvtColor(processed_array, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR)
                
                out.write(processed_bgr)
                processed_count += 1
                
                if processed_count % 30 == 0:
                    print(f"Processed {processed_count}/{total_frames//frame_skip} frames")
            else:
                out.write(frame)
        
        cap.release()
        out.release()
        print(f"Video processing complete! Saved to: {output_path}")


# Interactive visualization tool
class InteractiveVisualizer:
    """Interactive tool for exploring activation maximization patterns."""
    
    def __init__(self, device='cuda'):
        """
        Args:
            device: Computing device
        """
        self.device = device
        self.current_pattern = None
        self.current_result = None
    
    def explore_features(self, model, layer_name, num_filters=64):
        """
        Interactively explore feature visualizations.
        
        Args:
            model: Neural network model
            layer_name: Layer to visualize
            num_filters: Number of filters to explore
        """
        visualizer = FeatureVisualizer(model, layer_name, self.device)
        
        print(f"\nExploring {num_filters} filters from layer '{layer_name}'")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        rows = int(np.sqrt(num_filters))
        cols = (num_filters + rows - 1) // rows
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, cols, figsize=(cols*2, rows*2))
        axes = axes.flatten() if num_filters > 1 else [axes]
        
        for i in range(num_filters):
            print(f"Visualizing filter {i+1}/{num_filters}...", end='\r')
            img = visualizer.visualize_filter(
                filter_index=i,
                iterations=20,
                lr=0.1
            )
            axes[i].imshow(img)
            axes[i].set_title(f'F{i}', fontsize=8)
            axes[i].axis('off')
        
        # Hide extra subplots
        for i in range(num_filters, len(axes)):
            axes[i].axis('off')
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(f'feature_exploration_{layer_name}.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.show()
        print(f"\nSaved: feature_exploration_{layer_name}.png")
    
    def compare_attacks(self, image, model, target_class):
        """
        Compare different adversarial attacks.
        
        Args:
            image: Input PIL Image
            model: Target model
            target_class: Target class for attacks
        """
        adv_gen = AdversarialExampleGenerator(model, self.device)
        
        attacks = {
            'FGSM (ε=0.01)': lambda: adv_gen.fgsm_attack(image, target_class, epsilon=0.01),
            'FGSM (ε=0.03)': lambda: adv_gen.fgsm_attack(image, target_class, epsilon=0.03),
            'FGSM (ε=0.05)': lambda: adv_gen.fgsm_attack(image, target_class, epsilon=0.05),
            'I-FGSM': lambda: adv_gen.iterative_fgsm_attack(image, target_class, epsilon=0.03),
            'PGD': lambda: adv_gen.pgd_attack(image, target_class, epsilon=0.03),
            'DeepFool': lambda: adv_gen.deepfool_attack(image, num_classes=10),
        }
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 10))
        axes = axes.flatten()
        
        for idx, (name, attack_fn) in enumerate(attacks.items()):
            print(f"\nGenerating {name} attack...")
            adv_img = attack_fn()
            
            results = adv_gen.evaluate_attack(image, adv_img, target_class)
            
            axes[idx].imshow(adv_img)
            axes[idx].set_title(
                f'{name}\n'
                f'Pred: {results["adversarial_prediction"]}\n'
                f'L2: {results["l2_norm"]:.4f}, '
                f'PSNR: {results["psnr"]:.1f}dB',
                fontsize=9
            )
            axes[idx].axis('off')
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig('attack_comparison.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.show()
        print("\nSaved: attack_comparison.png")


# Performance benchmarking
class PerformanceBenchmark:
    """Benchmark different activation maximization patterns."""
    
    def __init__(self, device='cuda'):
        """
        Args:
            device: Computing device
        """
        self.device = device
        self.results = {}
    
    def benchmark_pattern(self, pattern_name, pattern_fn, num_runs=5):
        """
        Benchmark a specific pattern.
        
        Args:
            pattern_name: Name of the pattern
            pattern_fn: Function to execute
            num_runs: Number of runs for averaging
        """
        import time
        
        times = []
        memory_usage = []
        
        print(f"\nBenchmarking {pattern_name}...")
        
        for run in range(num_runs):
            # Clear cache
            if torch.cuda.is_available():
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()
                torch.cuda.synchronize()
            
            # Measure time
            start_time = time.time()
            
            # Execute pattern
            _ = pattern_fn()
            
            if torch.cuda.is_available():
                torch.cuda.synchronize()
            
            end_time = time.time()
            elapsed = end_time - start_time
            times.append(elapsed)
            
            # Measure memory
            if torch.cuda.is_available():
                memory = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 1024**2  # MB
                memory_usage.append(memory)
                torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
            
            print(f"  Run {run+1}/{num_runs}: {elapsed:.2f}s", end='')
            if memory_usage:
                print(f", {memory:.1f}MB")
            else:
                print()
        
        self.results[pattern_name] = {
            'avg_time': np.mean(times),
            'std_time': np.std(times),
            'avg_memory': np.mean(memory_usage) if memory_usage else 0,
            'std_memory': np.std(memory_usage) if memory_usage else 0,
        }
    
    def print_results(self):
        """Print benchmark results."""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("BENCHMARK RESULTS")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"{'Pattern':<30} {'Time (s)':<15} {'Memory (MB)':<15}")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        for pattern, results in self.results.items():
            time_str = f"{results['avg_time']:.2f} ± {results['std_time']:.2f}"
            mem_str = f"{results['avg_memory']:.1f} ± {results['std_memory']:.1f}"
            print(f"{pattern:<30} {time_str:<15} {mem_str:<15}")
        
        print("=" * 80)

    synthesized_img.save('workflow_texture.jpg')
    
    # Step 6: Generate adversarial examples
    print("\nStep 6: Generating adversarial examples...")
    classifier = models.resnet18(pretrained=True)
    adv_gen = AdversarialExampleGenerator(classifier, device)
    
    # Get original prediction
    orig_tensor = adv_gen._preprocess_image(input_img)
    with torch.no_grad():
        output = classifier(adv_gen.normalize(orig_tensor))
        orig_class = output.argmax(dim=1).item()
    
    target_class = (orig_class + 100) % 1000
    adv_img = adv_gen.pgd_attack(input_img, target_class, epsilon=0.03)
    adv_img.save('workflow_adversarial.jpg')
    
    # Step 7: Create comparison visualization
    print("\nStep 7: Creating comparison visualization...")
    processed_imgs = [dream_img, stylized_img, synthesized_img, adv_img]
    titles = ['DeepDream', 'Style Transfer', 'Texture Synthesis', 'Adversarial']
    compare_results(input_img, processed_imgs, titles, 'workflow_comparison.png')
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("WORKFLOW COMPLETE!")
    print("=" * 80)
    print("\nGenerated files:")

    print("  - workflow_dream.jpg")
    print("  - workflow_stylized.jpg")
    print("  - workflow_texture.jpg")
    print("  - workflow_adversarial.jpg")
    print("  - workflow_comparison.png")

# Error handling and validation utilities
class PatternValidator:
    """Validate inputs and outputs for activation maximization patterns."""
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_image(image, min_size=32, max_size=2048):
        """
        Validate image input.
        
        Args:
            image: PIL Image or path
            min_size: Minimum image dimension
            max_size: Maximum image dimension
            
        Returns:
            PIL Image
            
        Raises:
            ValueError: If image is invalid
        """
        if isinstance(image, str):
            if not os.path.exists(image):
                raise ValueError(f"Image file not found: {image}")
            image = Image.open(image)
        
        if not isinstance(image, Image.Image):
            raise ValueError("Input must be PIL Image or file path")
        
        width, height = image.size
        if width < min_size or height < min_size:
            raise ValueError(f"Image too small. Minimum size: {min_size}x{min_size}")
        if width > max_size or height > max_size:
            raise ValueError(f"Image too large. Maximum size: {max_size}x{max_size}")
        
        return image
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_model(model):
        """
        Validate model input.
        
        Args:
            model: PyTorch model
            
        Raises:
            ValueError: If model is invalid
        """
        if not isinstance(model, nn.Module):
            raise ValueError("Model must be a PyTorch nn.Module")
        
        # Check if model has parameters
        if sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) == 0:
            raise ValueError("Model has no parameters")
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_device(device):
        """
        Validate and get appropriate device.
        
        Args:
            device: Device string ('cuda', 'cpu', or 'auto')
            
        Returns:
            Valid device string
        """
        if device == 'auto':
            return 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
        elif device == 'cuda' and not torch.cuda.is_available():
            print("Warning: CUDA not available, using CPU")
            return 'cpu'
        return device
    
    @staticmethod
    def check_output_quality(original, processed, min_psnr=20):
        """
        Check quality of processed image.
        
        Args:
            original: Original PIL Image
            processed: Processed PIL Image
            min_psnr: Minimum acceptable PSNR
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with quality metrics
        """
        orig_array = np.array(original).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
        proc_array = np.array(processed).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
        
        # Ensure same size
        if orig_array.shape != proc_array.shape:
            proc_array = np.array(processed.resize(original.size)).astype(np.float32) / 255.0
        
        # Calculate MSE
        mse = np.mean((orig_array - proc_array) ** 2)
        
        # Calculate PSNR
        if mse > 0:
            psnr = 10 * np.log10(1.0 / mse)
        else:
            psnr = float('inf')
        
        # Calculate SSIM (simplified version)
        def ssim_channel(img1, img2):
            c1 = 0.01 ** 2
            c2 = 0.03 ** 2
            
            mu1 = np.mean(img1)
            mu2 = np.mean(img2)
            sigma1 = np.var(img1)
            sigma2 = np.var(img2)
            sigma12 = np.mean((img1 - mu1) * (img2 - mu2))
            
            ssim = ((2 * mu1 * mu2 + c1) * (2 * sigma12 + c2)) / \
                   ((mu1**2 + mu2**2 + c1) * (sigma1 + sigma2 + c2))
            return ssim
        
        if len(orig_array.shape) == 3:
            ssim = np.mean([
                ssim_channel(orig_array[:,:,i], proc_array[:,:,i])
                for i in range(orig_array.shape[2])
            ])
        else:
            ssim = ssim_channel(orig_array, proc_array)
        
        quality = {
            'mse': mse,
            'psnr': psnr,
            'ssim': ssim,
            'acceptable': psnr >= min_psnr
        }
        
        return quality


# Configuration management
class PatternConfig:
    """Configuration manager for activation maximization patterns."""
    
    # Default configurations for each pattern
    DEFAULTS = {
        'feature_visualization': {
            'iterations': 30,
            'learning_rate': 0.1,
            'img_size': 224,
            'regularization_weight': 1e-4
        },
        'deepdream': {
            'iterations': 20,
            'learning_rate': 0.01,
            'octave_scale': 1.4,
            'num_octaves': 4
        },
        'style_transfer': {
            'num_steps': 300,
            'style_weight': 1000000,
            'content_weight': 1,
            'learning_rate': 0.003
        },
        'texture_synthesis': {
            'output_size': (512, 512),
            'num_steps': 500,
            'learning_rate': 0.01
        },
        'adversarial': {
            'epsilon': 0.03,
            'alpha': 0.01,
            'num_iterations': 40
        }
    }
    
    def __init__(self, pattern_type):
        """
        Args:
            pattern_type: Type of pattern
        """
        self.pattern_type = pattern_type
        self.config = self.DEFAULTS.get(pattern_type, {}).copy()
    
    def update(self, **kwargs):
        """Update configuration parameters."""
        self.config.update(kwargs)
    
    def get(self, key, default=None):
        """Get configuration value."""
        return self.config.get(key, default)
    
    def save(self, filepath):
        """Save configuration to JSON file."""
        import json
        with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(self.config, f, indent=2)
    
    @classmethod
    def load(cls, filepath, pattern_type):
        """Load configuration from JSON file."""
        import json
        config = cls(pattern_type)
        with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
            loaded_config = json.load(f)
        config.config.update(loaded_config)
        return config

## README and Documentation

```python
"""
================================================================================
ACTIVATION MAXIMIZATION PATTERNS - COMPREHENSIVE DOCUMENTATION
================================================================================

OVERVIEW
--------
This module provides complete implementations of 5 activation maximization
patterns in PyTorch for understanding and manipulating neural network behavior.

PATTERNS INCLUDED
-----------------

1. FEATURE VISUALIZATION
   - Visualizes what patterns maximally activate specific neurons
   - Useful for understanding what features a network has learned
   - Applications: Model interpretability, debugging, education

2. DEEPDREAM
   - Creates dream-like hallucinogenic images
   - Amplifies patterns detected by neural networks
   - Applications: Art generation, understanding network perception

3. NEURAL STYLE TRANSFER
   - Transfers artistic style from one image to another
   - Preserves content while applying style
   - Applications: Artistic effects, image stylization

4. TEXTURE SYNTHESIS
   - Generates new textures from example textures
   - Uses neural network feature statistics
   - Applications: Texture generation, material design, graphics

5. ADVERSARIAL EXAMPLE GENERATION
   - Creates inputs that fool neural networks
   - Multiple attack methods: FGSM, I-FGSM, PGD, C&W, DeepFool
   - Applications: Security testing, robustness evaluation

INSTALLATION
------------
pip install torch torchvision pillow matplotlib numpy

Optional dependencies:
pip install opencv-python  # For video processing

QUICK START
-----------

# Feature Visualization
from activation_patterns import FeatureVisualizer
visualizer = FeatureVisualizer(model, 'layer_name', device='cuda')
img = visualizer.visualize_filter(filter_index=0)

# DeepDream
from activation_patterns import DeepDream

result = dreamer.dream(image, layers=['conv_3', 'conv_4'])

# Style Transfer
from activation_patterns import NeuralStyleTransfer

result = transfer.transfer_style(content_img, style_img)

# Texture Synthesis
from activation_patterns import TextureSynthesizer
synthesizer = TextureSynthesizer(device='cuda')
texture = synthesizer.synthesize(texture_img, output_size=(512, 512))

# Adversarial Examples
from activation_patterns import AdversarialExampleGenerator
adv_gen = AdversarialExampleGenerator(model, device='cuda')
adv_img = adv_gen.fgsm_attack(image, target_class=100)

PERFORMANCE TIPS
----------------
- Use GPU (CUDA) for 10-100x speedup
- Reduce iterations for faster prototyping
- Use smaller image sizes during development
- Enable mixed precision training for memory efficiency
- Batch process multiple images when possible
- Clear CUDA cache between operations if memory limited

MEMORY OPTIMIZATION
-------------------
- Reduce image resolution: 224x224 instead of 512x512
- Lower number of octaves in DeepDream (2-3 instead of 4-5)
- Reduce optimization steps: 100 instead of 300
- Process images sequentially instead of in batch
- Use torch.cuda.empty_cache() between operations
- Enable gradient checkpointing for large models

QUALITY VS SPEED TRADEOFFS
--------------------------
Pattern              | Fast (Low Quality) | Balanced      | High Quality
---------------------|-------------------|---------------|---------------
Feature Viz          | 10 iter, lr=0.2   | 30 iter, lr=0.1 | 100 iter, lr=0.05
DeepDream            | 5 iter, 2 octaves | 20 iter, 4 oct  | 50 iter, 6 oct
Style Transfer       | 50 steps          | 300 steps       | 1000 steps
Texture Synthesis    | 100 steps         | 500 steps       | 2000 steps
Adversarial (FGSM)   | epsilon=0.01      | epsilon=0.03    | epsilon=0.05

COMMON PARAMETERS
-----------------
iterations/num_steps: Number of optimization iterations
  - More = better quality but slower
  - Typical range: 10-1000

learning_rate/lr: Step size for gradient updates
  - Higher = faster convergence but less stable
  - Typical range: 0.001-0.1

epsilon: Perturbation magnitude for adversarial attacks
  - Larger = more visible but more effective
  - Typical range: 0.01-0.1

style_weight: Importance of style vs content
  - Higher = stronger style transfer
  - Typical range: 1e5-1e7

TROUBLESHOOTING
---------------

Problem: Out of memory error
Solution: 
  - Reduce image size
  - Lower batch size
  - Use CPU instead of GPU
  - Clear CUDA cache: torch.cuda.empty_cache()

Problem: Poor quality results
Solution:
  - Increase iterations
  - Adjust learning rate
  - Try different layers
  - Check input image quality

Problem: Slow processing
Solution:
  - Use GPU if available
  - Reduce image resolution
  - Lower number of iterations
  - Use quick demo mode

Problem: Adversarial attack not working
Solution:
  - Increase epsilon
  - Use iterative methods (PGD) instead of FGSM
  - Try different target classes
  - Increase number of iterations

Problem: Style transfer looks unnatural
Solution:
  - Adjust style_weight (try lower values)
  - Increase content_weight
  - Use different style layers
  - Try more optimization steps
